Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt, is the giver of venerable wealth. Worship Indra himself, the delightful and great-souled, for protection.
notes: ಶಾದ್ರ್ಮನಿಗೆ: garbled word after ಇಂದ್ರನೊಡನೆ ಸ್ನೇಹಸಂಪಾದನೆಗಾಗಿ

en: Your priests, (oh worshippers), propitiate Indra for his friendship, offering great (praise), and desirous of his favour; for the wielder of the thunderbolt is the giver of vast (wealth); worship him, therefore, who is mighty and benevolent, (to obtain) his protection.

Sāyaṇa says: in which Indra the riches that are good for men are poured in, that is, are filled (an active form used in a passive sense by a change of voice). If one asks where in Indra, it is in his hand, that is, his arm. Or else this word is an adjective of Indra in the same case: the slayer, Indra in whom. Yāska has said: "hasta is from han, quick in striking" (Ni. 1-7). Or else, the riches that rest in this Indra are poured in, that is, filled, by the praisers. And the Indra who is by nature a stander in the chariot sits in a golden chariot. Or else, the riches, standing as if in the chariot, remain in the golden chariot, and that Indra pours, showers. And of whom the thick, extended arms (gabhasti is a name of the arm) have the reins, the bridles, poured in, that is, held. And of whom the horses, showerers and young, yoked to the chariot, come, fill, on the road. We praise that Indra: this is the part to be supplied.
- यस्मिन् हस्ते (*yasmin haste*)—in the hand of which Indra
- रथेष्ठाः (*ratheṣṭhāḥ*)—which Indra, who is by nature a stander in the chariot
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—and fit to be yoked to the chariot

Worship that Indra in whose hand riches good for mankind are filled; who, being by nature a stander in the chariot, sits in a golden chariot; in whose extended arms the bridles of the horses are held; and whose horses, powerful and of themselves fit to be yoked to the chariot, overrun the very road.

In whose hand (riches) good for man are accumulated, the chariot-mounted in a golden car; in whose arms the rays of light (are collected); whose vigorous horses, yoked (to his car, convey him) on the road (of the firmament).

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, for prosperity, that is, for wealth, they pour on your feet service, that is, they offer it; Bharadvāja offers it (the plural is used by a change of number). Or else, your two feet, to be resorted to, to be served, for prosperity, they pour service, that is, they perform it. You who, by might, by strength, are the overpowerer of enemies, the bearer of the thunderbolt,

the possessor of the dakṣiṇā, the wealth to be given to the praisers, O leader Indra, you, to be seen by all, clothe yourself, cover yourself, in your own form, excellent (praiseworthy) and ever in motion, like the sun, and have become desirable, or going. The word कमिति (*kamiti*) is a filler.
- दक्षिणावान् (*dakṣiṇāvān*)—you who possess wealth to be given
- अत्मं (*atmaṃ*)—the form that ever moves about
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—so as to be seen by all

O Indra, Bharadvāja offers worship at your feet for the gaining of prosperity. O Indra, leader of rites, you, by your strength the overpowerer of enemies, the bearer of the thunderbolt, the possessor of wealth to be given, wearing a praiseworthy form that ever moves about, so as to be seen by all, have become revolving like the sun.

They offer adoration at your feet to acquire prosperity, for you are the overthrower of enemies by (your) strength, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bestower of donations ; leader (of rites), you are like the rolling sun, wearing in the sight (of all) a graceful and ever-moving form.

Sāyaṇa says: that Soma, of which mention is made, when pressed became most perfectly mixed, mixed face to face, that is, it unites most closely with Indra. When this Soma has been pressed, the things to be cooked, the cake and the rest, are cooked; the fried barley, the grains, are there, prepared for the oblation. And when this Soma has been pressed, the leaders, the priests who are makers of the brahma, that is, of the food of the nature of the oblation, praising Indra with hymns and reciting (pronouncing) the uktha-verses and the śastras, become most eminently near to the gods. The construction is: that Soma became mixed with Indra.
- धानाः (*dhānāḥ*)—grains of barley and the like
- संति (*saṃti*)—are prepared (and when which juice is pressed)
- देववाततमाः (*devavātatamāḥ*)—and becoming those who obtain the nearness of the gods
- सः सोमः (*saḥ somaḥ*)—that same Soma juice
- आमिश्लतमः भूत् (*āmiślatamaḥ bhūt*)—becomes that which joins Indra

When which Soma juice is pressed, the cake is cooked for the offering of the oblation, and grains such as barley are prepared; and when which juice is pressed, the priests, who are leaders and praisers, become praisers of Indra, reciters of the śastras, and obtainers of the nearness of the gods: that same Soma juice, pressed, joins Indra.
That libation is most perfectly mixed when, upon its being effused, the cakes are baked, and the barley is fried, and the priests, glorifying
Indra, offering the (sacrificial) food, and reciting holy prayers, are approaching most nigh to the gods.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, no end, no limit, of this strength of yours, of the qualities stated, has been established; here the simple root is to be understood as having the sense of the root with the prefix before it, so that the meaning is that it has not been known by us. By the greatness of which strength heaven and earth are quickly shaken; that is, heaven and earth are afraid of that strength. That strength the praiser, hastening, worshipping fully with the satisfying oblation, fills up. The illustration: as a cowherd, giving water to the herds of cows in the waters, satisfies them with the waters, so does the praiser.
- न धायि (*na dhāyi*)—has not been determined
- यूथेव (*yūtheva*)—as one satisfies herds of cows with water

O Indra, no one can know the limit of your well-known strength. Even heaven and earth are afraid because of your greatness. As a cowherd, in the midst of water, satisfies the herds of cows with water, so your praiser, performing the sacrifice with satisfying oblations, satisfies your powers.

No limit of your strength has been assigned; heaven and earth are intimidated by its greatness: the pious worshipper, hastening (to sacrifice), and earnestly performing worship, gratifies you with the offering, as (the cowkeeper satisfies) the herds with water.

Sāyaṇa says: in the manner so stated, may the mighty Indra be easily invoked, that is, easy to be called. The word इत् (*it*) is a filler. Hariśipra: the śipras are the jaws or the nostrils; he whose śipras are of tawny colour ⟨NOTE:3⟩. Such an Indra, by coming or by not coming, becomes the bringer of riches: whether he has come himself or not, he gives wealth to the praisers. Thus born, that is, manifested, this Indra, being one whose strength is unequalled, incomparable and most excellent, destroys many obstructors, the Rākṣasas and the like; and may he also destroy the Dasyus, the destroyers, and the enemies.
notes: ಹಿರಿಶಿಪ್ರಃ: Sāyaṇa glosses tawny (harita) colour, the Kannada Pratipadārtha has ನೀಲವರ್ಣದ ಕೆನ್ನೆ "blue-coloured cheek"

en: - सत्वा (*satvā*)—may he be the giver of wealth
- एवा हि (*evā hi*)—in this very manner
- असमात्योजाः (*asamātyojāḥ*)—being one of most excellent strength

May the great Indra be favourable to our invocation and accept it. May Indra, with blue-coloured cheeks, be the giver of wealth to us, whether by his coming or without coming. In this very manner may Indra, who has appeared, being one of most excellent strength, destroy the Asuras, who are exceedingly numerous.

Thus may the mighty Indra be successfully invoked; he, the azure-chinned, the giver of wealth, whether by coming or nnt coming (to the sacrifice); and may he who is of unequalled strength destroy, as soon as manifested, many opposing (evil spirits) and (hostile) Dasyus.

Sāyaṇa says: this Indra grew exceedingly, he became greatly strong. For what purpose? For heroic deeds, to do heroic acts such as the slaying of Vṛtra. The sole chief, undecaying one, who cannot be made to grow old, that Indra gives riches, he gives them to the praisers. Further, this Indra surpasses heaven and earth, he exceeds them. And of this Indra ⟨NOTE:4⟩
both heaven and earth are only a half: the half portion of this Indra becomes the counterpart of heaven and earth.
notes: ಕಿಂಜಾಸ್ಯೇಂದ್ರ-: garbled word at the page end; read here as "and of this Indra"

en: - प्र रिरिचे (*pra ririce*)—has surpassed and grown
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- अर्धमिश् प्रति (*ardhamiś prati*)—are in greatness only the measure of a half

Indra has grown again and again to accomplish his heroic deeds. Indra, the chief and free from old age, gives riches. He has grown beyond the heavenly world and the earthly world. Heaven and earth are, for this Indra, only the measure of a half in greatness.

Again has Indra increased (in strength) for (the display of) heroism : he, the chief (of all), the undecayable, bestows riches (on his votaries); Indra surpasses heaven and earth: a mere portion of him is equal to both earth and heaven.

Sāyaṇa says: now I praise this Indra's great strength, skilled in the slaying of Asuras; the word मन्यतिः (*manyatiḥ*) is a word for praise ⟨NOTE:5⟩. And whatever deeds he has upheld, these no one diminishes, no one harms. And what are they? It is told: day after day the sun, enveloped by Vṛtra, became visible, that is, becomes visible; by the slaying of the obstructing Asura he made the sun shine: this is one deed. The Indra of good deeds extended the worlds, wide and spacious; he made them: this is another deed. The meaning is that he did many deeds, beginning with these.
notes: ಸೌಮಿ: garbled word before ಮನ್ಯತಿಃ ಸ್ತುತಿಕರ್ಮಾ

en: - दर्शतः भूत् (*darśataḥ bhūt*)—becomes visible to all (by the grace of Indra)
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—Indra, the doer of excellent deeds

I now praise the great strength of Indra, which destroys enemies. No one can harm the deeds of Indra. By the grace of this Indra the sun becomes visible to all every day. Indra, the doer of excellent deeds, has made all the worlds wide.

I now glorify his vast and Asura-destroying (vigour) : those exploits that he has determined (to achieve) no one can resist : (by him) the sun was made daily visible; and he, the doer of great deeds, spread out the spacious regions (of the universe).

notes: no Ṛk number printed after this Saṃhitā block; number 3 follows the sequence

en: Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, today and in earlier times too, that act of yours that belongs to the rivers continues: the act by which you cut a path, a way, for these rivers to flow, remains always unimpaired. Moreover, at your command the mountains have settled down: abandoning flight, they sat motionless in one place, like men sitting down for the sake of food that is to be eaten, who sit still for the sake of their meal. For this reason, O Indra of good deeds, by you all the worlds were made firm, made steady.
- अरदः (*aradaḥ*)—you made a way, the act so called
- अद्या चित् (*adyā cit*)—just as they are now
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—were well known in former times too
- अद्मसदो न (*admasado na*)—like men sitting motionless to eat food
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Indra, doer of excellent deeds
- दृळ्हानि (*dṛḷhāni*)—have been made to stand firm

O Indra, those acts of yours that belong to the rivers, the act so called of making a way for the rivers to flow, were well known in former times just as they are now. The mountains stand unmoving, like men sitting motionless to eat food. O Indra, doer of excellent deeds, by you alone all the worlds have been made to stand firm.
At present, verily as of old, that act, (the liberation) of the rivers, is effective ; whereby you have directed them on their course : the mountains
have settled (at your command) like (men) seated at their meals : doer of great deeds, by you, have the worlds been rendered stationary.
नू चित् (*nū cit*): the particle नू चित् (*nū cit*) is used when the matter of "new" and "old" is indicated. Yāska has given the explanation on this point:

नूचिदिति निपातः पुराणनवयोर्नूचेति च । अद्याचिन्नू चित्तदपो नदीनां । अद्य च पुरा च तदेव कर्म नदीनां । नू च पुरा च सदनं रयीणां रयिरिति धननाम रातेर्दानकर्मणः ॥ (*nūciditi nipātaḥ purāṇanavayornūceti ca | adyācinnū cittadapo nadīnāṃ | adya ca purā ca tadeva karma nadīnāṃ | nū ca purā ca sadanaṃ rayīṇāṃ rayiriti dhananāma rāterdānakarmaṇaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 4-17).

That is: having said that the particle नूचित् (*nūcit*) is used in the sense of new and old, he has given as an example the sentence in the present Ṛk, अद्याचिन्नु चित्तदपो नदीनां (*adyācinnu cittadapo nadīnāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-30-3). The action of the river, that is, the action of flowing, is of one kind both in former times and now. That is, the way the river used to flow in former times, so it flows now also: this is the meaning. And having said that the words नू च (*nū ca*) also are used in this same sense, for it he gives:

नू च पुरा च सदनं रयाणां जातस्य च जायमानस्य च क्षामं । सतश्च गोपा भवतश्च भूरेर्देवा अग्निं धारयन् द्रविणोदां ॥ (*nū ca purā ca sadanaṃ rayāṇāṃ jātasya ca jāyamānasya ca kṣāmaṃ | sataśca gopā bhavataśca bhūrerdevā agniṃ dhārayan draviṇodāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-7).
In this Ṛk, in the first pāda, the words नू च (*nū ca*) are used. O Agni, named Draviṇoda, you are, in former times and now, the resting place of wealth: this is the meaning.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, what is about to be said is true, truly so and not false: no other god like you exists; no other mortal, no man either, like you is found; no god or man who is greater, superior, exists. What is said thus is true: this is the meaning. Moreover, you slew the cloud, the serpent that lay encircling the water. And having slain it, you sent forth the waters toward the sea, the atmosphere or the ocean, facing it, that is, you let them go with their mouths turned downward.
- ज्यायान् (*jyāyān*)—no god superior to you: thus

O god, the saying that there is no god or man who is superior or equal to you is indeed true. You have slain the Asura named Vṛtra who lay encircling the water, and you have caused the waters of the atmosphere to flow in abundance.
Verily it is the truth, Indra, that there is no other such as you, no god nor mortal is (your) superior: you have slain Ahi obstructing the waters, you have set them free (to flow) to the ocean.

Sāyaṇa says: O Indra, you released the waters enclosed by Vṛtra in such a way that they flow in various directions, that is, spread out on all sides. For you broke open the firm place of the mountain, that is, of the cloud with its joints, which binds the waters. And you became king, lord, of the people of the world. Doing what? Bringing forth together, at one and the same time, the sun, the sky, the heavenly world, and the dawn, these three that were enveloped in darkness; that is, making them manifest, lighting them.
- दुरः (*duraḥ*)—which had been enclosed by Vṛtra
- विषोचीः (*viṣocīḥ*)—so that they spread everywhere and flow

O Indra, you released the waters that had been enclosed by Vṛtra, so that they spread everywhere and flow. You broke open the firm places of the cloud that bind them. Bringing forth together the sun, the heavenly world and the dawn, you have become lord over all the people of the world.

You have set the obstructed waters free to flow in all directions : you have fractured the solid (barrier) of the cloud ; you are lord over the people of the world, making manifest together the sun, the sky, and the dawn.

Sāyaṇa says: O lord of wealth, protector of wealth, Indra, you, the single chief, became the master of riches. Or else the connection is "lord of the riches": the word for wealth is repeated, as in यथा गवामसि गोपतिरेक इंद्र (*yathā gavāmasi gopatireka iṃdra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-98-6) ⟨NOTE:10⟩; then it is to be construed that you alone are the chief. And, O Indra, you hold in your two arms the peoples; that is, the whole world abides in your command. Further, men, in the matters of a son, of waters, of a hero, the impeller of enemies, and of grandsons, these being the occasions, utter various special praises, that is, they speak in manifold ways.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - रयिपते (*rayipate*)—O Indra, lord of all wealth
- आ अधिथाः (*ā adhithāḥ*)—you have lifted up and hold
- तोके (*toke*)—for the sake of a son
- तनये (*tanaye*)—for the sake of a grandson

O Indra, lord of wealth, you alone, the chief among the gods, have become the master of all riches. With your two arms you have lifted up and hold all the peoples (you protect them). Men, for the sake of a son, for the sake of water, and for the sake of valiant grandsons, recite in your name praises of many kinds.
You, lord of riches. are the chief (sovereign) over riches: you hold men in your two hands, and men glorify you with various praises for (the sake of obtaining) sons. and valiant grandsons, and rain.

O Indra, through fear of you the waters (the word for them is explained as the three worlds' waters) that belong to the earth and the mid-region, all-pervading, and by nature impossible to dislodge, are nevertheless made to move: the clouds shake them down; that is, they rain. Further, O Indra, when you come, heaven and earth, the mountains, and the forests, that is the trees, are seized with fear. Why say more: the whole visible, stable world of living creatures trembles. ⟨NOTE:11⟩
notes: ಅಚ್ಯುತಾ ಚಿತ್: Sāyaṇa takes the unshakeable waters as shaken down by the clouds; the Kannada Pratipadārtha/Bhāvārtha takes the clouds as the unmoving thing that is shaken

en: - अच्युता चित् (*acyutā cit*)—though devoid of movement
- च्यावयंते (*cyāvayaṃte*)—shake the clouds and cause rain to pour
- अ अज्मन् (*a ajman*)—at the time of coming

O Indra, through fear of you the three worlds, earth and the rest, all-pervading, shake the motionless clouds and cause rain to pour. At the time of your coming, heaven and earth, the mountains, the trees, and all stable things are seized with fear.

Through fear of you, Indra, all the regions of the firmament cause the unfallen (rain) to descend : the heavens, the earth, the mountains, the forests, all the solid (universe) is alarmed at your approach.

O Indra, you, together with Kutsa, fought against the asura named Śuṣṇa, who is unwithering, that is, impossible to wither, mighty, the one who withers everything; the meaning is that to help Kutsa you made war with that asura. Likewise in the *gaviṣṭi*: the "cows" are arrows, which go; hence *gaviṣṭi* is a battle.

In that battle you also slew the asura named Kuyava. Further, in the battle, the "falling" (*prapitva*), you carried off the wheel of the sun, a part of his chariot; from that time the sun's chariot has had one wheel. So it is handed down: सप्त युंजंति रथमेकचक्रं (*sapta yuṃjaṃti rathamekacakraṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.164-2). It is related that when the seer called Etaśa fought with the sun, Indra came to his help and took away the sun's wheel; and another passage of the Veda says: सूरश्चक्रं प्र वृहज्जात ओजसा (*sūraścakraṃ pra vṛhajjāta ojasā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-9). Moreover, you drove the sinful ones, the rākṣasas and the rest, away from this world; that is, you slew them.
- शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)—the asura called Śuṣṇa, facing him
- अभि युध्य (*abhi yudhya*)—you have waged war

O Indra, together with Kutsa you have waged war against the mighty asura called Śuṣṇa, facing him. In the battle for cows you have slain the asura called Kuyava. At the time of battle you have carried off the wheel of the sun, and you have driven the sinful rākṣasas far away.

You, Indra, with Kutsa, have warred against the inexhaustible Sushna: you have ovhrthrown Kuyava in battle : in conflict you have carried off the wheel (of the chariot) of the sun : you have driven away the malignant (spirits).

O Indra, you struck down the hundred cities of the Dasyu, the asura named Śambara, the destroyer; the cities were such that nobody could withstand them. O possessor of wisdom (*śacīvān*), O Sutakra, Indra, bought with the pressed Soma: at the time when you, by your wisdom, gave riches to Divodāsa who was pressing the Soma, and gave riches also to Bharadvāja who praises you, at that time you struck down the cities of Śambara. This is the construction.
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—to the one pressing the Soma juice
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—to the one who praises you
- अव जघंथ (*ava jaghaṃtha*)—you tore down and destroyed

O wise Indra, bought with Soma: at the time when you gave wealth, by your wisdom, to Divodāsa who presses the Soma juice, and gave riches to Bharadvāja who praises you, at that time you tore down and destroyed the hundred unassailable cities of the violent Śambara.

You have destroyed the hundred impregnable cities of the Dasyu, Sambara, when, sagacious Indra, you, who are brought by the libation, have bestowed in your liberality riches upon Divodasa presenting to you libations, and upon Bharadwaja hymning your praise.

O Indra, you whose warriors are true (*satyasatvan*), and whose wealth is abundant (*tuvinṛmṇa*): you, such as you are, mount your own formidable, terrible chariot for the great battle. O Indra of the excellent road (*prapathin*), come with that chariot, with your protection, towards me. And, O renowned Indra, make us heard of among the peoples, that is, make us famous; the meaning is: make us celebrated in the midst of all the subjects.
- सत्यसत्वन् (*satyasatvan*)—O you who have heroes of true strength
- तुविनृम्म (*tuvinṛmma*)—O Indra, possessor of abundant wealth
- प्रपथिन् (*prapathin*)—O Indra of the excellent road

O Indra, who have heroes of true strength and abundant wealth, mount and sit in your terrible chariot for the great battle. O Indra of the excellent road, come towards us together with your protection. O renowned Indra, make us famous before the other peoples.

Leader of true heroes, possessor of infinite wealth, mount your formidable car for the arduous conflict : come to me, pursuer of a forward path, for my protection: do you, who are renowned, proclaim (our renown) amongst men.

I fashion with my mouth for this Indra words of praise that are unprecedented, that is, new, not made by earlier singers; most numerous; and most productive of happiness. For what kind of Indra: great; a hero, the slayer of various enemies; mighty; swift; to be praised in a special degree ⟨NOTE:12⟩; the wielder of the thunderbolt; and grown great.
notes: ವಿರಪ್ಪಿನೇ in Saṃhitā, ವಿರಪ್ಯಿನೇ in Pada, ವಿರಷ್ಯನೇ in bhāṣya; readings differ

en: To Indra, who is of great nature, valiant, mighty, swift, greatly praised, the bearer of the thunderbolt, and growing in strength, I fashion from my mouth words of praise that are unprecedented (new), most abundant, and productive of happiness.
I have fabricated with my mouth unprecedented, comprehensive, and gratifying prasies to that mighty, heroic, powerful, rapid, adorable, and ancient wielder of the thunderbolt.

That Indra made the two mothers, heaven and earth, shine with the sun, for the sake of the far-seeing Aṅgirases. How did he do so? By splitting the mountain that had been set by force so that the cows could not be seen. Or else, the genitive "of the far-seeing Aṅgirases" stands for the instrumental sense, and the connection is: he was praised by the Aṅgirases. Further, he was repeatedly desired by the Aṅgirases, the singers, who are of good meditation, and so he released the confinement of the cows that had been carried off by the Paṇis, the servants of Vala.
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—with the help of the sun
- स्वाधीभिः (*svādhībhiḥ*)—by those intent on excellent meditation
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—and by the singers of praise, the Aṅgirases
- उस्रियाणां (*usriyāṇāṃ*)—of the cows that had been carried off

Indra, praised by the far-seeing Aṅgirases, splitting the mountain, made heaven and earth shine with the help of the sun. Desired again and again by the Aṅgirases, who are intent on excellent meditation and are singers of praise, he released the bond of the cows that had been carried off.

He has obtained :the parent (worlds, heaven and earth), with the sun, for the sake of the sages, (the Angirasas), and glorified (by them). he has shattered the mountain ; repeatedly wished for by his adorers intently meditating (upon him), he has cast off the fetters of the cows.

That Indra, the doer of many deeds, together with the Aṅgirases, bearers of the oblations, singers of praise, who always bend the knee, conquered the asuras on account of the cows. Having conquered, the destroyer of cities, Indra, wishing friendship with his friends, the Aṅgirases, who are of the same fame and far-seeing in wisdom, and being himself a seer, far-seeing in wisdom, broke the firm cities of the asuras.
- वह्निभिः (*vahnibhiḥ*)—with those who bear the oblations
- मितज्जुभिः (*mitajjubhiḥ*)—who bow down, kneeling, the Aṅgirases
- पुरोहा (*purohā*)—Indra, destroyer of the enemy's cities
- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—with those who are his friends
- कविः सन् (*kaviḥ san*)—himself also, being far-seeing

Indra, the doer of many deeds, together with the Aṅgirases, who bear the oblations, sing praises, and always bow down kneeling, conquered the asuras on account of the cows. Indra, the destroyer of the enemy's cities, desiring friendship with the Aṅgirases, his friends, who are far-seeing, and being himself far-seeing, destroyed the exceedingly hard cities of the enemy.

He, the achiever of many deeds, together with his worshippers ever offering oblations upon bended knees, has overcome (the Asuras) for (the rescue of) the cows: friendly with his friends (the Angirasas), far-seeing with the far-seeing, the destroyer of cities has demolished the strong cities (of the Asuras).

O showerer of desires, O Indra who are to be served with song, you, together with great food and great strengths, come, in the midst of the peoples, towards the praiser, with new mares that bring forth many heroes. What for? For a good thing, that is, for the attainment of happiness.
- पुरुवीराभिः (*puruvīrābhiḥ*)—accompanied by many heroes, with horses
- क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—in the midst of the peoples
- आ प्र याहि (*ā pra yāhi*)—be gracious and come

O Indra, showerer of desires and honoured with praises, with great foods and exceeding strengths, and with new horses accompanied by many heroes, be gracious and come, in the midst of the peoples, towards the praiser, for his welfare.
Showerer (of benefits), propitiated by praise, come to him who glorifies you, to make him happy amongst men with abundant food, with exceeding strength, and with young (mares) with numerous colts.

Indra, the overcomer of the violent, united with his strength that is always ready for action, and with swift horses or with ever-moving lights, in the southern course releases the waters; this is to be supplied. Thus released, those waters go each day to their goal, the ocean, which is not stirred by others, in such a way that there is no turning back, no return; they pervade it. ⟨NOTE:13⟩
notes: ಅಪ್ರಮೃಷ್ಯಂ: Sāyaṇa "not to be agitated by others"; Kannada "ಶೋಷ್ಯರಹಿತ" not to be dried up

en: - अप्रमृष्यं (*apramṛṣyaṃ*)—the ocean, which does not dry up

That same Indra, the assailer of enemies, united with horses, with his natural strength, released the waters in the southern course and made them flow. In this manner the waters, released from bondage, enter every day, without return, the ocean, their destination, which does not dry up.

Endowed with natural force, possessed of (swift) horses, Indra, the overcomer of adversaries, (sets free) the waters at the southern (declination): you liberated the waters expanded daily to the insatiable goal whence there is no returning.

O Indra, showerer of desires: give us well that son who is most mighty and strong, your gladdener, that is, one who delights you by his praises; of good purpose (*svabhiṣṭi*, "one whose seeking is fair") ⟨NOTE:15⟩; and a giver, that is, one who gives oblations. Give us a son endowed with such qualities, who, being possessed of good horses, shall in battles destroy the host of the enemy's good horses, and shall utterly overcome the obstructing enemies. This is the construction: give us him.
notes: ಸ್ವಭಿಷ್ಟಿಃ: Sāyaṇa "of good seeking"; Kannada "ಉತ್ತಮವಾದ ಯಜ್ಞಕರ್ತ" excellent sacrificer

en: - मदः (*madaḥ*)—a giver of delight to you by praise
- सौवश्वं (*sauvaśvaṃ*)—the good horses of the enemies

O Indra, showerer of desires: the son who is exceedingly mighty, a giver of delight to you by praise, an excellent sacrificer, and an offerer of oblations, and who, possessed of good horses, shall in battles destroy the enemies' good horses and defeat the hostile enemies: grant us such a son.

Showerer (of benefits), Indra, grant us a son who shall be most vigorous, a delighter (of you by praise), a pious sacrificer, a liberal giver, who mounted on a good steed, shall overthrow numerous good steeds, and conquer opposing enemies in combats.

O Indra, it is you alone whom men, who have various praises as their speech, call to their protection in the battle that is to be shared by heroes. And you, together with the wise Aṅgirases, destroyed the Paṇis, the asura followers of Vala; the meaning is that you slew them. Therefore the man who is protected by you, the one who shares in the worship, becomes one who obtains food.
- विनाचः (*vinācaḥ*)—men of various kinds of praises
- त्वोत इत् (*tvota it*)—only the man protected by you

O Indra, men who have various kinds of praises invoke you alone with prayer for protection in battle. You, together with the wise Aṅgirases, destroyed the Paṇis. Only the man protected by you, as your worshipper, obtains food.
Men of various speech invoke you, Indra, for their defence in war ; you, with the sages, (the Angirasas), have slain the Panis : protected by you, the liberal (worshipper) obtains food.

O Indra, you slew those enemies of both kinds. Which are the two kinds? The Dāsas, the destroyers, who are opposed to the rites, Vala and the other asuras; and the Āryas, who are excellent through the performance of rites, and the Vṛtras, the obstructers, Viśvarūpa and the others. Those enemies of both kinds, O hero, you have slain. O Indra, most leader-like among leaders, in battles you cleave with your well-placed weapons; you tear apart other enemies also. The illustration: like forests; as a man cuts the growths of trees with axes and the like, so you do. ⟨NOTE:16⟩
notes: ವೃತ್ರಾಣಿ: Sāyaṇa "obstructers, Viśvarūpa and others"; Kannada "ವ್ಯಾಪಕರೂ" pervading ones; ಆರ್ಯಾ: Sāyaṇa "excellent through performing rites", Kannada "belonging to the group of Āryas"

en: - आर्या (*āryā*)—those belonging to the group of the Āryas
- तान् उभयान् (*tān ubhayān*)—those two kinds of
- नृतम (*nṛtama*)—O Indra, the most excellent leader
- वनेव (*vaneva*)—as one splits trees with an axe
- आ दर्षि (*ā darṣi*)—you have split the enemies

O Indra, you have slain the enemies of two kinds: the Dasyus, who are opposed to the rites, and those belonging to the group of the Āryas devoted to the rites, and pervading ones. O Indra, the most excellent leader among leaders, in battles you have split the enemies with sharpened weapons, as one splits trees with an axe.

You, hero, Indra, destroyed both (classes of) enemies, (both) Dasa and Arya, adversaries; chief leader of leaders, you cut your foes in pieces in battles with well-pleid weapons, as (wood-cutters fell) the forests.

O Indra, such as you are, become the protector for our growth with unblamed protections. Likewise, be, as the one who goes everywhere, our friend. The word *nema* means "half"; it is said त्वो नेम इत्यर्थस्य (*tvo nema ityarthasya*) (Ni. 3-20). Battles are *nemadhiti*, because in them some half-number of men are laid down.
In such battles, fighting, we call you, O hero, to share in the choicest wealth, *svar*; whenever we call you, at that time be our protector and friend. This is the meaning.
- सः त्वं (*saḥ tvaṃ*)—you, such as you are
- स्वर्षाता (*svarṣātā*)—for the sake of the most excellent wealth

O Indra, famous as you are, be our protector, with your unblamed protections, for our growth. O valiant Indra, whenever, fighting in battles that destroy some men, we invoke you with prayer for the sake of the most excellent wealth, then, you who move everywhere, be our friend.

Do you, Indra, who are all-pervading, be a friend, and a protector with irreproachable protections for our prosperity; when warring in number-thinning conflicts, we invoke you for the acquirement of wealth.

O Indra, be ours now, today; and in another time also be ours. Moreover, when we come to you, be gracious, a giver of happiness to us. Thus praising, we, who are great winners of cows, may we abide in the happiness that belongs to you, the great, in the shining and grief-removing refuge.
- अपराय च (*aparāya ca*)—at another time also be belonging to us
- अभिष्टौ (*abhiṣṭau*)—as the giver of what is desired

O Indra, be ours now and at other times as well. Be the giver of what is desired and a giver of happiness to us. Thus praising, may we, as worshippers of cows, abide in the happiness that belongs to you, the great, which is shining and destroys grief.

Do you, Indra, now and at (all) other times be verily ours: be the bestower of happiness according to our condition : and in this manner, worshipping at dawn, and glorifying you, may we abide in the brilliant and unbounded felicity of you who are mighty.
O Indra, many words, that is, praises, come together in you. From you wide-ranging thoughts of the singers, that is, their minds, go forth in many ways. In earlier time, and today, of the seers…

The sense of the sentence begun before: the praises, that is, the hymns, of the seers who see beyond the senses, Bharadvāja and the others, vie with one another in excess for Indra (पस्पृध्रे (*paspṛdhre*) means "they vied"). The meaning is that each, saying "I first, I first", became eager in praising Indra. In the same sense the Ṛk speaks of the ukthārkā: ukthā is the śastra (recitation), and its forms, the arkas, the instruments of worship, that is, the hymns, also vied.
- वि यंति (*vi yaṃti*)—unfold in many ways
- ऋषीणां (*ṛṣīṇāṃ*)—of the seers, Bharadvāja and the others
- उत्थार्का (*utthārkā*)—the ukthā mantras, instruments of worship (also vie)

O Indra, praises of many kinds come together in you alone. The minds of the singers, wide-ranging as they are, unfold in many ways from you alone. Now and in former time the hymns of the singers, Bharadvāja and the others, vie in excess in the very praising of Indra. The ukthā mantras, instruments of worship, likewise vie.

Many praises, Indra, are concentrated in you : from you abuandent commendations diversely proceed : to you, formerly and at present, the praises of the sages, their prayers and hymns, vic (in glorifying) Indra.

Indra is "invoked by many" (पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)), "extolled by many" (पुरुगूर्तः (*purugūrtaḥ*), lifted up by many), "mighty" (ऋभ्वा (*ṛbhvā*), great) and "the one" (एकः (*ekaḥ*), the chief). The Indra of such qualities who is praised in many ways by sacrifices (यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)), that is, by the sacrificers, the men, or by the hymns that are the means of sacrifice, that Indra, like a chariot, is yoked for great strength (शवसे (*śavase*)), that is, joined to that purpose by our praises, and may he be worthy of being gladdened (अनुमाद्यः (*anumādyaḥ*)) by us, the singers. May he always be one to be praised.
- पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)—one who is called by many
- पुरुगूर्तः (*purugūrtaḥ*)—one who is worshipped by many

May that Indra, who is called by many, worshipped by many, great, and the chief among all the gods, and who is honoured in excess by the sacrificers, be praised at all times by us, the singers, joined with our praises for great strength, like a chariot.

May that Indra ever be propitiated by us who is the invoked of many, mighty and chief, especially honoured by sacrifices, and to whom, as to a conveyance, we are attached for (the attainment of) great strength.

The Indra whom the dhītayaḥ, that is, rites and services, do not harm, do not oppress; and whom the vāṇīḥ, the words, the praises, do not oppress. A man who is unable to give is greatly distressed by services and praises made by others. But because of this Indra's abundance of wealth and his being a giver, the services and hymns offered to him do not become causes of distress. What then? Making that Indra grow, they reach him (अभि नक्षंति (*abhi nakṣaṃti*), they go to him). Moreover, if a hundred singers praise Gīrvaṇas, the sharer of praises (गिर्वणसं (*girvaṇasaṃ*)), and if a thousand singers praise him, all that praise is शं (*śaṃ*), that is, productive of happiness, for this Indra.
- गिर्वणिसं (*girvaṇisaṃ*)—towards Indra, who is worthy of worship through praise
- यदि गृणंति (*yadi gṛṇaṃti*)—if they offer praise and extol

Whichever Indra neither the acts of worship nor the words of praise harm, going to that Indra and making him grow, all those praises reach him. The hundreds and thousands of praisers who extol that Indra and offer him praises of many kinds, all those praises are productive of happiness for that Indra.

All praises contributing to his exaltation proceed to Indra, whom no acts, no words can harm, since hundreds and thousands of adorers glorify him who is entitled to praise, and so afford him gratification.

"On this day", that is, on the day of the pressing of Soma, अर्चेव (*arceva*), as if with a hymn that is the instrument of worship, मासा (*māsā*), with a measure, that is, joined with a mantra to be accomplished by the words beginning "Indrāya tvā vṛtraghne", the Soma, sprinkled with the waters called vasatīvarī and ekadhanā, is held fast in this Indra (a change of case is to be understood: अस्मै (*asmai*) for "in this"). Or else the meaning is: "To this Indra I would speak this hymn", the words "I would speak" being supplied. Another explanation: दिवि (*divi*), in the heavenly world, अर्चेव (*arceva*), like the sun; मासा (*māsā*) (the elliptical simile), the moon, which measures; like him, the sprinkler of rain and waters, who is Indra, in this Indra the pressed Soma is held fast. Moreover, the hymns together with the oblations, the puroḍāśa cakes and the rest, which are the means of sacrifice, made that Indra grow together.

Here is the illustration. धन्वन् (*dhanvan*), in a desert land, अभि (*abhi*), towards a man, the waters flowing together well, as a living being is, that is, as waters found in a desert land make a living being grow, so (the hymns make Indra grow).
- अर्चेव (*arceva*)—like a hymn that is the instrument of worship
- मिमिक्षः (*mimikṣaḥ*)—that which is joined with the vasatīvarī waters
- जनं न (*janaṃ na*)—as it gladdens him
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—joined with oblations, the means of sacrifice
notes: ಮಾಸಾ — ಧ್ಯಾನಾತ್ಮಕವಾದ ಮಂತ್ರದಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿದುದೂ: Sāyaṇa explains māsā as "with a measure" or as the moon

en: The Soma, which is joined with a meditative mantra like a hymn that is the instrument of worship, and with the vasatīvarī waters, is offered today in this Indra. As the water flowing before a traveller in a sandy desert gladdens him, the hymns joined with oblations, the means of sacrifice, gathering together, made that Indra grow.

The mixed Soma juice has been prepared for Indra, (to be offered) on the day (of sacrifice), with reverence-like adoration, when praises, together with offerings, yield him increase, as when water (revives) a man in a desert waste.

To this Indra this great (महि (*mahi*)) āṅgūṣa hymn has been spoken (अवाचि (*avāci*)) by the minds, that is, by the singers. The repetition "to this Indra the hymn" is for the sake of reverence. May that Indra, who goes everywhere (विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)), in the great, abundant vṛtratūrya, the battle, be our protector and the one who makes us grow, in such a manner (यथा (*yathā*)) was the hymn spoken: this is the construction.
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—the one who makes us grow
Because Indra, who goes everywhere, is our protector and the one who makes us grow in the great battle, this great hymn has been recited by the praisers, addressed to this Indra.
To this Indra has this earnest eulogy been addressed by the devout, in order that the all-pervading Indra may be our defender and exalter in the great conflict with (our) foes.

O Indra, when will our hymns (ब्रह्म (*brahma*), that is, our praises), which have the chariot for their dwelling (रथक्षयाणि (*rathakṣayāṇi*)), come to be? The meaning is: when will they reach you as you stand on the chariot? When will you give me, who praise you, the सहस्रपोष्यं (*sahasrapoṣyaṃ*), that is, a herd of cattle or a son that nourishes a thousand persons? When will you make this hymn of mine, the singer's, pervade (वासयः (*vāsayaḥ*)) with wealth? And when will you make my rites, such as the agnihotra and the rest (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)), delightful with food (वाजरत्नाः (*vājaratnāḥ*), delightful with vāja, that is, with food)? Thus the singer, unable to bear the delay of the fruit, asked Indra with this Ṛk.
- रथक्षयाणि (*rathakṣayāṇi*)—as dwelling in your chariot (with you)
- सहस्रपोष्यं (*sahasrapoṣyaṃ*)—wealth that nourishes thousands of people

O Indra, when will our hymns reach you, who stand on the chariot? When will you give to me, the singer, wealth that nourishes thousands of people? When will you make the praise of me, the singer, fruitful with wealth? When will you make our rites delightful with food?

When may our prayers (be with you) in your chariot? when will you grant to your adorer the i(means of) maintaining thousands? when will you recompense my adoration with riches? when will you render sacred rites productive of food?

The seer, unable to bear the delay of the fruit, asks Indra with this Ṛk also. O Indra, "when indeed" (कर्हि स्वित् (*karhi svit*)) would that be, that you bring together (नीळयासे (*nīḷayāse*)) with our men the enemy men, and with our heroes, that is, our sons, the enemy heroes and sons? The root नीळयतिः (*nīḷayatiḥ*) has the sense of joining. Such a joining in battle, when would it be? so runs the question. Moreover, when will you win the battles for us? And when will you win in addition (अधि जयासि (*adhi jayāsi*)) the cattle that are found among the enemies who approach the cow-pen, cattle that bear the three threefold products (त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*): milk, curds and ghee)? O Indra, when will you place among us pervading (स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*)) wealth (द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*), that is, riches)?
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—(bringing face to face) the enemy men
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—(bringing face to face) the enemy heroes
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever effort for battle there is
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—having the substance of milk and the rest
- अधि जयिसि (*adhi jayisi*)—will you win for us?

O Indra, when will you bring our heroic men together with the enemy heroes and make ready for battle? And when, causing the effort for battle to be made, will you bring us victory? When will you win for us and bring the cattle that are among the enemies who oppose us, cattle that have the three substances beginning with milk? O Indra, when will you establish all-pervading wealth in us?

When, Indra, will you bring together leaders with leaders, heroes with heroes, and give us victory in battles? when will you conquer from the enemy the threefold food-supplying cattle? (when will you grant) us, Indra, diffusive wealth?

With this Ṛk also some questions are put. O Indra, when indeed would that be? O Śaviṣṭha, most mighty Indra, that you make (कृणवः (*kṛṇavaḥ*)) for the singer, the praiser, food (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)) of many forms (विश्वप्सु (*viśvapsu*)): when would that be? so runs the question. And when will you join (युवासे (*yuvāse*)) to yourself our rites (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) and the praises (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)), the word न (*na*) being in the sense of combination? And when will you approach (गच्छाः (*gacchāḥ*)) our hymns (हवनानि (*havanāni*)), which are givers of cattle (गोमघा (*gomaghā*))? The word मघा (*maghā*) is a form of the root meaning "to give", standing as the last member of the compound. ⟨NOTE:18⟩
notes: ಗೋಮಘಾ ... ಗಚ್ಛಾಃ: the Kannada gloss renders ಗಚ್ಛಾಃ "will you make fruitful with the gift of wealth", while Sāyaṇa's ಅಭಿಗಚ್ಛೇಃ means "will you approach"

en: - कर्हि स्मित् (*karhi smit*)—when indeed (will you bring about)

O mighty Indra, the matter that is famed, that you make for him who praises you a wealth of food of many forms: when will you bring it about? When will you unite our rites and our praises in yourself? When will you make our hymns fruitful with the gift of wealth?

When most vigorous Indra, will you grant your worshipper that food which is all-sufficing ? whea will you combine (in yourself) worship and praises ? when will you render oblations productive of cattle ?

O Indra, you, for the singer, the praiser, place (धेहि (*dhehi*), bestow) in us, the sons of Bharadvāja, foods (पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*)) that are givers of cattle (गोमघा (*gomaghā*)), delighting with horses (अश्वश्चंद्रा (*aśvaścaṃdrā*)) and famed for strength (वाजश्रवसः (*vājaśravasaḥ*)). And, O Indra, nourish (पीपिहि (*pīpihi*), make swell) those foods and the cow, the well-milking one (सुदुघां धेनुं (*sudughāṃ dhenuṃ*)). And make them shine (रुरुच्याः (*rurucyāḥ*)) in such a way that they become of beautiful radiance (सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*)): the meaning is, let them be endowed with beautiful radiance.
- गोमघाः (*gomaghāḥ*)—those that furnish wealth of cattle
- भरद्वाजेषु (*bharadvājeṣu*)—in us, the sons of Bharadvāja
- सुदुघां धेनुं (*sudughāṃ dhenuṃ*)—the cows that are excellent milkers

O Indra, fill in us, the sons of Bharadvāja, for the singer, the foods that furnish wealth of cattle, are delightful with horses and are famed for strength. O Indra, make those foods and the cows that are excellent milkers thrive. Make them radiant, so that they shine exceedingly.

Grant Indra, to your adorer (abundant) food, productive of cattle, pleasant with horses, and renowned for vigour: multiply nourishment, and (cherish) the cows easily milked, and render them so that they may be resplendent.

O Indra, you now (नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)) bring our present obstructing enemy (वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)) to a different (अन्यथा (*anyathā*)) manner: that is, to a manner unlike that in which all live, the one called death. The syllable आ (*ā*) is a filler. O Śakra, Indra, capable in all works, brave and endowed with heroism, tearing the enemies apart in an especial manner (वि दुरः (*vi duraḥ*)). Or else: breaking open the doors belonging to the enemy. Since you are praised (गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)) by us, for that reason may I not go away (मा निररं (*mā niraraṃ*)) from the hymn, the speech, the cow of Indra, the milker of the pure and spotless (शुक्रदुघस्य (*śukradughasya*)). Or else: the milker of the pure milk, of the cow given by you.

(So that) I may not depart from the vicinity of the cow. The word "aram" is a verb, a form of the root meaning "to go". The meaning is: may she always dwell among us. O Vipra, wise Indra, gratify (जिन्व (*jinva*), that is, please) with food (ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)) us, the Āṅgirasas, those born in the lineage of Aṅgiras.
- सूनं (*sūnaṃ*)—that which is of this time
- अन्यथा चित् आ (*anyathā cit ā*)—make him one whose attention is elsewhere, or make him dead
- विदुरः (*viduraḥ*)—and destroyer of enemies, you are (therefore)
- शुक्रमघस्य (*śukramaghasya*)—of Indra, whose wealth is pure
- मा निररं (*mā niraraṃ*)—may I not become averse
- अंगिरसान् (*aṃgirasān*)—us, who are born in the lineage of Aṅgiras

O Indra, turn the enemies who are present at this time of the sacrifice in another direction. O almighty Indra, for whatever reason you are mighty and the destroyer of enemies, for that very reason you are praised. For that reason, may I not become averse to the praise of Indra, whose wealth is pure. O wise Indra, make us, who are born in the lineage of Aṅgiras, rich in food, and satisfy us.

Direct him who is actually our adversary into a different (course): mighty Indra, you are a hero, the destroyer (of enemies). therefore are you glorified : never may I desist from the praise of the giver of pure (gifts): satisfy ; sage Indra, the Angirasas with food.

O Indra, your intoxications (मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)) produced by the drinking of Soma are सत्रा (*satrā*), which is a name for "truth": truly they are beneficial to all people (विश्वजन्याः (*viśvajanyāḥ*)). Or else: सत्रा (*satrā*) is a name for "great", and the construction is "your intoxications are great". Moreover, the riches (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)), the masses of wealth that are yours and are पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*), that is, found in the three worlds designated by the earth, they too truly are beneficial to all people: this is the construction. Further, you truly are (अभवः (*abhavaḥ*), you become) the distributor (विभक्ता (*vibhaktā*)), the giver, of foods (वाजानां (*vājānāṃ*)). Or else the construction is "of great foods". Since you hold strength (असुर्यं (*asuryaṃ*)) among the gods, for that reason you act so: this is the meaning.
- मदासः (*madāsaḥ*)—the satisfactions born of drinking Soma
- पार्थिवासः (*pārthivāsaḥ*)—those that are in the three worlds
- ये रायः (*ye rāyaḥ*)—whatever riches of yours there are (those also)
- विभक्ता अभवः (*vibhaktā abhavaḥ*)—you become the distributor

O Indra, the satisfaction born of your drinking of Soma brings benefit to the whole world. Your riches, spread through the three worlds, are truly beneficial to the world. By that greatness of yours by which you hold strength among the gods, for that very reason you are truly the distributor of foods.

Truly are your exhilarations beneficial to all men: truly are the riches which exist on earth (beneficial to all men): truly are you the distributor of food ; therefore you maintain vigour amongst the gods.

The worshipper (जनः (*janaḥ*)), the sacrificer, continually and eminently worships (अनु प्र येजे (*anu pra yeje*)) the strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)) of this Indra. Moreover, the sacrificers truly place him before them (अनु दधिरे (*anu dadhire*)) in order to perform a heroic deed. Or else the construction is "the great Indra". And further, to him who seizes (सूमगृभे (*sūmagṛbhe*)) the enemies that go on without interruption, to the destroyer (दुधये (*dudhaye*); the root has the sense of harming: दुधिर्हिंसाकर्मा (*dudhirhiṃsākarmā*)) of them, and to the one who goes against the enemies (अर्वते (*arvate*)), to that Indra they perform (वृंजंति (*vṛṃjaṃti*), accomplish) the rite (क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)) consisting of service. For what purpose? For the slaying (वृत्रहत्ये (*vṛtrahatye*)) of Vṛtra, the obstructing enemy. ⟨NOTE:20⟩
notes: ಸೂಮ್ನಃ ಸೂತಾನವಿಚ್ಛೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಾನ್ ಶತ್ರೂನ್: the reading of ಸೂಮ್ನಃ is doubtful; rendered after the Kannada "ಅನುಸೂತವಾಗಿ ಬರುವ ಶತ್ರುಗಳನ್ನು"

en: - अनु प्र येजे (*anu pra yeje*)—worships always
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—for the performance of heroic deeds
- अनु दधिरे (*anu dadhire*)—they worship, setting him as the model
- सूमगृभे (*sūmagṛbhe*)—who seizes the enemies that come in succession
- अर्वते (*arvate*)—the one who defeats the enemies; (addressing) that Indra

The sacrificer always worships the strength of Indra. The sacrificers, in order to perform heroic deeds, worship Indra truly, setting him as the model. They offer worship to that Indra, who takes captive the enemies that press on without a break, who harms the enemies and defeats the enemies, for the destruction of the enemies.

The worshipper praises especially the strength of that Indra, verily they rely upon him for heroic deeds: they offer sacrifices to him as the seizer of an uninterrupted series of foes their assailant, their subduer, and also for their destruction.

That Indra the Maruts, moving together (सध्रीचीः (*sadhrīcīḥ*)), that is, assembled, attend (सश्चुः (*saścuḥ*), serve) for his protection. Or else: the ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*), the satisfying foods, being together, serve him. Likewise the virile powers (वृष्ण्यानि (*vṛṣṇyāni*)) and strengths (पौंस्यानि (*pauṃsyāni*)), and the mares (नियुतः (*niyutaḥ*)) yoked to the chariot, serve that Indra. Moreover the praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) whose strength is the recitation (उक्षशुष्मा (*ukṣaśuṣmā*): उक्तं (*uktaṃ*) is the śastra, and that itself is their strength) enter (आ विशंति (*ā viśaṃti*)) that Indra, who is of wide extent (उरुव्यचसं (*uruvyacasaṃ*)). Here is an illustration: as rivers (सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)), which are flowing by nature, enter the ocean (समुद्रं न (*samudraṃ na*)) and, having entered, are no longer seen as distinct, so all the praises become one with Indra: this is the meaning.
notes: ಊತಯಃ—ಮರುತ್ತುಗಳೂ: the Kannada gloss takes ಊತಯಃ as the Maruts; Sāyaṇa takes ಸಧ್ರೀಚೀಃ as the Maruts, or ಊತಯಃ as foods

en: - समुद्रं न (*samudraṃ na*)—as they go and join the ocean
- उक्तशुष्माः (*uktaśuṣmāḥ*)—the recited mantras full of strength

The Maruts, the companions of Indra, the virile powers, the strengths and the horses of Indra serve Indra together. As rivers enter the ocean, the recited mantras full of strength and the praises go and join the widely pervading Indra.
The associated Maruts, heroic energies, virile strength, and the Niyut steeds, attend upon Indra, and praises powerful in sacred song centre in him as rivers flow into the ocean.

O Indra, you who are praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)), of wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) the खां (*khāṃ*): खा (*khā*) is a name for rivers, and here the stream connected with it is meant. उप सृज (*upa sṛja*): release the stream, join it with us. Of what kind of wealth? पुरुश्चंद्रस्य (*puruścaṃdrasya*), which gladdens many, and वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*), which gives dwelling. Moreover you, incomparable (असमः (*asamaḥ*)) and supreme, have become the lord, the overlord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)), of all people, all beings (जनानां (*janānāṃ*)); and likewise of the whole world (विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (*viśvasya bhuvanasya*)), of all that is born, you have become the one, the unique, king and ruler.
- वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*)—and is the cause of dwelling
- खां (*khāṃ*)—the stream in the form of a flood
- असमः (*asamaḥ*)—as the one without a second
O Indra, you who are praised by all, cause to flow the stream, in the form of a flood, of wealth that gives joy to many and is the cause of dwelling. You, the one without a second
and lord of creatures. You are the sole master of the whole of created beings.
Glorified by us. Indra, let flow the stream of much-delighting, home-conferring affluence, for you are the unequalled lord of men, the sole sovereign of all the world.

"O Indra, listen quickly to the praises that are fit to be heard (श्रुत्या (*śrutyā*) is explained as श्रुत्यानि शोतव्यानि (*śrutyāni śotavyāni*), praises to be heard); you who, desiring our service, overcome like the sun the abundant riches belonging to the enemy, be that one and hear." The construction is: you who do so, listen. Further: you, endowed with your own strength and being praised, and made known age after age by the offered food, the oblation; as you are not common but peculiarly ours, so may you be. ⟨NOTE:22⟩
notes: ಅರ್ಯೋರೇಃ in Sāyaṇa's block looks damaged (Kannada gloss ಶತ್ರುವಿನ "of the enemy"); ಹನಿರ್ಲಕ್ಷಣೇನ read as havir-lakṣaṇena; the closing ಅಸಃ । ಸ್ಯಾಃ is as printed

en: - वयसा (*vayasā*)—by the food in the form of the oblation
- असः (*asaḥ*)—be favourable; be in that way

O Indra, you who, desiring our acts of worship, seize abundantly the riches of the enemy like the sun, listen quickly to our praises. Being endowed with strength, praised by us, and made known by us at all times through food in the form of the oblation, be in whatever way is favourable to us.

Hear, Indra, (the praises) that may be heard (by you), who, are gratified by our adoration, and, like the sun, (prevail) over the ample riches of the enemy : endowed with strength, being glorified in every age rendered comprehensible by (sacrificial) food, be to us no other (than such as you have been.)

O fierce Indra, of uplifted strength, may your horses, yoked to the chariot, bring your chariot, which all desire (विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*), to be chosen by all), towards us. For (हि (*hi*)) the praiser, the seer Bharadvāja, who possesses स्वः (*svaḥ*) (explained as a group of qualities, and he is endowed with it), invokes you; for that reason may they bring your chariot towards us. And we also, today, rejoicing together with you, would prosper. ⟨NOTE:23⟩
notes: Sāyaṇa's ಸ್ವಃ ಸುಷ್ಕರಣೇಯಂ ಗುಣಜಾತಂ looks damaged; the Kannada gloss ಸ್ವರ್ವಾನ್ "endowed with devotion" differs

en: - विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)—worthy of the regard of all

O Indra, of fearful power, may the horses yoked to your chariot bring your chariot, which is worthy of the regard of all, towards us. Bharadvāja, who is endowed with devotion and is the praiser, calls you. May we too, experiencing common joy with you, attain prosperity.
Fierce Indra, let your harnessed steeds bring down your all-desired chariot : your devoted adorer verily invokes you: may we to-day, partaking of your exhilaration, increase to-day (in prosperity).

In the third paryāya, this Ṛk, प्रो द्रोण (*pro droṇa*), is the śastra-yājyā of the Acchāvāka priest. It is also taught in the sūtra: "प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*)", with the reference Ā. 6-4. The green Soma juices (हरयः (*harayaḥ*)) come forward to our rite (कर्म (*karma*), our sacrifice); having come they are purified in the pitcher (द्रोणे (*droṇe*), the Droṇa vessel) and, flowing straight (ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*)), become so. The ancient (पूर्व्यः (*pūrvyaḥ*)) Indra, who abides in radiance or dwells in the heavenly region, and who is the lord of the exhilarating Soma, may drink this Soma.
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the Soma juices of green hue
- प्रो अग्मन् (*pro agman*)—come forward and join
- द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)—the radiant dweller of the heavenly region

The Soma juices of green hue come forward to our sacrifice. Then, purified, they join together in the Droṇa vessel. May Indra, the ancient one, the radiant dweller of the heavenly region, the lord of the gladdening Soma juice, drink this Soma.

The green Soma juices flow at our sacrifice, and, purified, proceed direct into the pitcher: may the ancient. illustrious Indra, the sovereign of the exhilarating Soma libation, drink of this our offering.

In the third paryāya the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this Ṛk, प्रो द्रोणे (*pro droṇe*), as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्निति याज्या (*pro droṇe harayaḥ karmāgmanniti yājyā*) (Ā. Sū. 6-4).

The horses yoked to the chariot (रथ्यासः (*rathyāsaḥ*)), going about on every side (आसस्राणासः (*āsasrāṇāsaḥ*)), moving straight (ऋज्यंतः (*ṛjyaṃtaḥ*), going directly), should carry towards our oblation, which is to be heard of (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)), Indra, who stands in the chariot with fair wheels (सुचक्रे (*sucakre*)) and acts like strength itself (शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)). The word नू चित् (*nū cit*) is a particle used here in the sense of negation. The immortal (अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)), that is the oblation consisting of Soma, which is not the cause of death, should not be wasted, should not come to destruction by the wind: Soma taken in a vessel dries up through the wind; therefore, before that happens, the horses should bring Indra to drink it. ⟨NOTE:24⟩
notes: ಆಸಸ್ರಾಣಾಸಃ in Sāyaṇa's block begins ಅಸಸ್ರಾಣಾಸಃ; the passage ರ್ವಾಯೋರ್ಹೇತೋನು is damaged and its construction is not certain

en: - सुचक्रे (*sucakre*)—in the chariot with excellent wheels
- शवसानं (*śavasānaṃ*)—who is the representative of strength
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—the Soma, which is like ambrosia
- वायोः (*vāyoḥ*)—by the force of the wind
- विदस्यॆत् (*vidasyèt*)—let it not be dried up

May the horses, moving about everywhere and yoked to the chariot, going straight, bring Indra, the representative of strength, in the chariot with excellent wheels, towards the oblation. May the Soma, which is like ambrosia, not be dried up and wasted by the force of the wind.
May the everywhere-going, straight-proceeding, chariot-bearing steeds, bring the mighty Indra in his strong-wheeled car to our rite : let not the ambrosial Soma waste in the wind.
In this Ṛk the companionship of Indra and Vāyu is described. In many contexts Indra and Vāyu have the same kind of epithets. To support this point Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:

आसस्यवांसोऽभिबलायमानमिंद्रं कल्याणचक्रे रथे योगाय रथ्या अश्वा रथस्य वोढार ऋज्यंत ऋजुगामिनोऽन्नमभिवहेयुर्नवं च पुराणं च । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सतः । वायोश्चास्य भक्षो यथा न विदस्येदिति । इंद्रप्रधानेत्येके नैघुंटुकं नायुकर्मोभयप्रधानेत्यपरं ॥ (*āsasyavāṃso 'bhibalāyamānamiṃdraṃ kalyāṇacakre rathe yogāya rathyā aśvā rathasya voḍhāra ṛjyaṃta ṛjugāmino 'nnamabhivaheyurnavaṃ ca purāṇaṃ ca | śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ | vāyoścāsya bhakṣo yathā na vidasyediti | iṃdrapradhānetyeke naighuṃṭukaṃ nāyukarmobhayapradhānetyaparaṃ ‖*)

That is: the horses that draw Indra's chariot, ever moving about, bring Indra, who is exceedingly mighty and sits in the chariot with excellent wheels, to partake of the old and the new food (the Soma). Indra's horses are by nature ones that go straight, that is, without turning this way or that, only facing forward. The intention is: that the Soma juice prepared for Indra may not dry up and be wasted through the drying power of the wind, may the horses bring Indra here quickly and straight. The word श्रवः (*śravaḥ*) is a synonym among the names of food. Because food is well known, food is also called श्रवः (*śravaḥ*). May the Soma not dry up and be wasted through the drying power of the wind. Some hold that in this Ṛk the matter of Indra is presented as the principal one; others hold that it is the action of Vāyu that is presented, and that both are praised.

Indra is वरिष्ठ (*variṣṭha*), the most excellent, and तुविकूर्मितमः (*tuvikūrmitamaḥ*), one who performs exceedingly many kinds of deeds. Among the wealthy (मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*), those possessed of wealth in the form of oblations) he sends forth (इयर्ति (*iyarti*), impels) the fee (दक्षिणां (*dakṣiṇāṃ*)) that is to be given at the sacrifice of this sacrificer. Or else: मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*) agrees with अस्य (*asya*) through a change of number, so that the sense is: of this sacrificer, who is rich in oblations; the rest is evident. O wielder of the thunderbolt, by the fee given you remove the sin connected with the sacrifice (परियासि (*pariyāsi*) means: you destroy it). O bold one, the destroyer of enemies, with which fee you grant riches and सूरीन् (*sūrīn*), praisers and sons, such a fee you send forth. ⟨NOTE:25⟩
notes: ಸ್ತೋತ್ಥಾನ್ and ಧೃಷ್ಟೋ read as printed

en: - धृष्णो (*dhṛṣṇo*)—and humbler of the pride of enemies, O Indra

O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt and humbler of enemies, by what giving of wealth you destroy sin, and by what act of giving you favour us with riches and with sons who are praisers, such wealth fit to be given you, the most excellent, the doer of manifold deeds, the lord of all, provide for this sacrificer among the wealthy.

The very strong Indra, the performer of many great deeds, instigates the donation of this (institutor of the ceremony) amongst the opulent, whereby, wielder of the thunderbolt, you remove sin, and, firm of purpose, bestow riches upon the worshippers.

May this Indra be the giver of स्थविरस्य वाजस्य (*sthavirasya vājasya*), abiding food, that is, strength. And may that Indra, of greatly increased splendour (वृद्धमहाः (*vṛddhamahāḥ*)), grow by our praises. सत्वा (*satvā*) means the chastiser of enemies: may that Indra be हनिष्ठः (*haniṣṭhaḥ*), the best slayer, of Vṛtra, the enemy who obstructs. And the impeller (सूरिः (*sūriḥ*)), that Indra, hastening (तूतुजानः (*tūtujānaḥ*) is explained as one who hurries), fills up those riches: may he give them to us. ⟨NOTE:26⟩
notes: ಬಲಸ್ಯ ನಾ ದಾತಾ in the block: ನಾ unclear

en: - आ पृणति (*ā pṛṇati*)—let him give to us

May Indra be the giver of abiding food. And, being of exceeding splendour, may he grow by our praises. May Indra, the destroyer of enemies, destroy the enemy in the form of Vṛtra. May Indra, the impeller, hastening, give us the well-known riches.

Indra is the donor of substantial food: may the very illustrious Indra increase (in glory) through our praises: may Indra, the destroyer (of enemies), be the especial slayer of Vritra : may he, the animator, the quick-mover, grant us those (riches which we desire).

That Indra, who is चित्रतमः (*citratamaḥ*) (the most worthy of being gathered to, or the most wonderful), अपात् (*apāt*): may he drink Soma from this vessel of ours, the grahacamasa and the like (इतः (*itaḥ*)). Or else: may he protect us (अपात् (*apāt*) is पातु (*pātu*), रक्षतु (*rakṣatu*)) from this enemy. उदु (*udu*) are two expletives. Likewise may that Indra bear (भर्षत् (*bharṣat*) is बिभर्तु (*bibhartu*), धारयतु (*dhārayatu*)) the great, shining invocation of Indra, that is, praise. In the course (यामन् (*yāman*)) of the sacrifice of the devout man (the one belonging to the gods), may Indra, the good giver (सुदानुः (*sudānuḥ*)), enjoy (संभजतु (*saṃbhajatu*)) the most praiseworthy rite performed in the sacrifice, in the form of service (धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)), and the gift (रातिं (*rātiṃ*)), the oblation fit to be offered. ⟨NOTE:27⟩
notes: ಪತ್ಯಸೀಂ for ಪನ್ಯಸೀಂ and ವನಶೇ for ವನತೇ in the block read as printed

en: - इतः (*itaḥ*)—from our cups and other vessels
- राशिं (*rāśiṃ*)—and the oblation fit to be given

May Indra, the most attractive, drink from our cups and other vessels the Soma offered by us. May he bear the great and radiant praise addressed to Indra. Indra, the excellent giver, enjoys in the sacrifice of the sacrificer who belongs to the gods the praiseworthy act of worship and the oblation fit to be given.

May the most marvellous Indra drink from this (our cup) : may he acknowledge our earnest and brilliant invocation: may the munificent (Indra) accept the offering and the praiseworthy adoration at the sacrifice of the devout worshipper.

The two ears of this Indra, even from a distant place, come (आ वसतः (*ā vasataḥ*): they come to hear the praise). Because of the praise to be proclaimed (घोषात् (*ghoṣāt*)) of Indra, the praiser, reciting (ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*), praising), makes sound (तन्यति (*tanyati*)); or else: he spreads it everywhere. देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*) is this praise, in the form of an invocation of the god Indra, and being herself urged on (ऋच्यमाना (*ṛcyamānā*)), may she turn this Indra to face me (मद्यक् (*madyak*), towards me); इयं (*iyaṃ*) is to be repeated. ⟨NOTE:28⟩
notes: Kannada ಆ ವಸತಃ ವಾಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೂ "though dwelling" differs from Sāyaṇa ಆಗಚ್ಛತಃ "come"; ಮದ್ರಕ್/ಮದ್ಯಕ್ for ಮದ್ರ್ಯಕ್ as printed

en: - घोषात् (*ghoṣāt*)—for the sake of the praise
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—that which invokes the god Indra
- आ ववृत्यात् (*ā vavṛtyāt*)—let it make him turn

Though Indra is very far away, the praiser, reciting praise, makes sound addressed to him, so as to touch Indra's ears. May this praise that invokes the god Indra, self-impelled, make this Indra turn towards me.

Reciting (his praise, the worshipper) calls aloud, that by the sound he may reach the ears of Indra, although abiding afar off: may this invocation of the deity, inducing him (to come). bring Indra to my presence.

"O Indra, that such Indra" तं (*taṃ*): the plural वः (*vaḥ*) stands by a change of number. I praise (अभ्यनूषि (*abhyanūṣi*)) him with the most excellent praise (परमयोत्कृष्टतमया धिया (*paramayotkṛṣṭatamayā dhiyā*)) together with oblations (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*), the means of worship). Of what kind is he: पुराजां (*purājāṃ*), born in former time, ancient; अजरं (*ajaraṃ*), free from old age, eternal. For that reason, in this Indra the oblations in the form of food (ब्रह्म (*brahma*)) and the praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) are joined together (सं दधिरे (*saṃ dadhire*), they are put together, they cling), and the great, swelling praise (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)) grows further. ⟨NOTE:29⟩
notes: ತಂ ತಾದೃಶಮಿಂದ್ರಂ ವಸ್ತಾಂ in the block: ವಸ್ತಾಂ unclear; ಇಂದ್ರೆ for ಇಂದ್ರೇ as printed

en: - अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)—and with oblations, the means of worship
- अस्मिन् इंद्रे (*asmin iṃdre*)—in this very Indra
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the food in the form of oblation

O Indra, you who are ancient, free from old age and lord, that same you I worship with the most excellent praise and with oblations that are the means of worship. In this very Indra the food in the form of oblation and the praises have come together. Very great praise also grows exceedingly.
I glorify you with hymns and with pious worship, the ancient undecaying Indra, for in him are oblations and praises concentrated, and great adoration is enhanced (when addressed to him).

The Indra whom the sacrifice (यज्ञो (*yajño*), the rite) makes grow (वर्धात् (*vardhāt*)); and also Soma, the means of it, makes that Indra grow. So too ब्रह्म (*brahma*), food in the form of the oblation, such as the sacrificial cake and the like, makes that Indra grow. The praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)) and the मन्म (*manma*), the thoughtful recitations of the śastra kind, make him grow. This Indra the Dawns (उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)) cause to grow when the night (अक्टोः (*akṭoḥ*)) goes on (यामन् (*yāman*)). The months, the autumns, that is, the years, and the days make this Indra grow. ⟨NOTE:30⟩
notes: ಮನನೀಯಾನ್ಕುಕ್ಷೋಕಶಸ್ತ್ರಾಣೆ in the block looks damaged (perhaps ukthaśastrāṇi)

en: - ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—and the food in the form of oblation
- उक्ता (*uktā*)—and the recited mantras, make whom strong
- यामन् (*yāman*)—in the time of its passing

The Indra whom the sacrifice, the Soma that is its means, and the food in the form of oblation make full-grown, and whom the praises and the recited mantras that serve meditation make strong: that same Indra the Dawns make grow in the time of the night's passing. The months, the years and the days are causes of Indra's growth.
Indra, whom the sacrifice, whom the libation exalts, whom the oblation, the praises, the prayers, the adoration exalt, whom the course of day and night exalts, whom months, and years, and days exalt.

O wise (विप्र (*vipra*), intelligent) Indra, you who are thus (एव (*eva*)) being born, manifesting yourself (जज्ञानं (*jajñānaṃ*)), for the overcoming of enemies (सहसे (*sahase*)), असामि (*asāmi*), abundantly, growing (वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*)), great (महां (*mahāṃ*)), mighty (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), of uplifted strength): you do we serve (विवासेम (*vivāsema*), परिचरेम (*paricarema*)) today in the battles in which Vṛtra is slain (वृत्रतूर्येषु (*vṛtratūryeṣu*)), for renowned (श्रुताय (*śrutāya*)) wealth (राधसे (*rādhase*)) and for protection (अवसे (*avase*)).
- जज्ञानं (*jajñānaṃ*)—one who has come into being
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—and one of fearful strength, you

O wise Indra, you who have thus come into being, who have grown exceedingly in order to defeat the enemies, a great soul, one of fearful strength, we worship in the battles, for fame, for wealth and for protection.

So, wise Indra, may we to-day propitiate you who are manifested. to overcome (our foes), you who are greatly augmenting, mightly and free, for (the sake of) wealth, fame, and protection, and for the destruction of (our) enemies.

मंद्रस्य (*maṃdrasya*) is delighting or intoxicating; कवेः (*kaveḥ*), the powerful; दिव्यस्य (*divyasya*), born in heaven; वह्नेः (*vahneḥ*), the bearer; विप्रमन्मनः (*vipramanmanaḥ*) is one whose praisers (मन्मनः (*manmanaḥ*)) are the wise (विप्रा (*viprā*)); वचनस्य (*vacanasya*), that which is to be spoken of, to be praised; that which is famed everywhere; सचनस्य (*sacanasya*), to be served; the sweet Soma (मध्वो मधुनः सोमस्य (*madhvo madhunaḥ somasya*)) of such a kind, our Soma, O Indra, you drink (अपाः (*apāḥ*), पिब (*piba*)). The genitive here stands in the sense of the dative, since the act of taking is to be performed on it as the thing given. And, O shining god Indra, to me who praise (गृणते (*gṛṇate*); the dative stands for the instrumental), join (युवस्व (*yuvasva*), संयोजय (*saṃyojaya*)) foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*), foods) that have cattle at their head. ⟨NOTE:31⟩
notes: ಗೋಅಗ್ರೀ ಪ್ರಮುಖೇ in the block looks damaged

en: - गो अग्राः (*go agrāḥ*)—having cattle as the chief part

O Indra, drink the sweet Soma juice, offered by us, intoxicating, life-giving, born in the heavenly world, bearing fruit, meditated on by the praisers, praiseworthy, well known and fit to be served. O shining Indra, join to me, the praiser, foods that have cattle as their chief part; that is, fill me with all of them.

Drink, Indra, of that our sweet, exhilarating, inspiring, celestial, fruit-yielding Soma, commended by the wise, and entitled to praise and preparation: bestow upon him who glorifies you, divine (Indra), food, the chiefest of which is cattle.

This Indra, desiring (उशानः (*uśānaḥ*)) the cows (उस्रा (*usrā*)) that were near the mountain (अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)), the mass of rock made by Vala to enclose the cows, joining (युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)) the Aṅgirases whose acts were true (ऋतधीतिभिः (*ṛtadhītibhiḥ*)), and being joined with the praise (ऋतयुक् (*ṛtayuk*)) made by them, broke (वि रुजत् (*vi rujat*)) the unbroken (अरुग्णं (*arugṇaṃ*)) summit (सानुं (*sānuṃ*)), the high mountain belonging to the asura Vala. And further, the Paṇis, the asuras of that name who were Vala's followers, Indra fought (अभि योधत् (*abhi yodhat*)) with words alone (वचोभिः (*vacobhiḥ*)), words that were praiseworthy and warlike, in the nature of संतर्जन (*saṃtarjana*).
- यतधीतिभिः (*yatadhītibhiḥ*)—with the Aṅgirases, whose acts are true
- सानुं (*sānuṃ*)—the high part of the mountain

Wishing to obtain the cows that were around the mountain made by Vala to confine the cows, Indra joined the Aṅgirases, whose acts are true, and, furnished with praise, split apart the high part of the mountain of the asura Vala, which others could not enter. He confronted the Paṇis, the followers of Vala, with harsh words alone.

Determined (to recover) the cattle hidden in the mountain, associated with the celebrators of pure rites, (the Angirasas), and animated by (their) veracious (praise), this (Indra) fractured the infrangible rock of Vala. and overwhelmed the Panis with reproaches.

O Indra, this Indu, Soma, controlled (नियम्यमानः (*niyamyamānaḥ*)) or drunk by you, illumined (वि द्योतयत् (*vi dyotayat*)) the dark (अद्युतः (*adyutaḥ*)) अक्तून् (*aktūn*). अक्तुरिति (*akturiti*) is a name of night; here, by association with it, fortnights, months and the like are meant. So Soma illumined the fortnights, months and the like, the night (दोषा (*doṣā*)), the day (वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)), the autumns, that is, the years. Why? Because the gods formerly (नू चित् (*nū cit*)) set up (अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)) this Soma, which stands in the sky in the form of the moon, as the indicator (केतुं (*ketuṃ*)) of the days (अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*)), and therefore by it all fortnights, months and the like are made known, since the divisions of the lunar days depend on the moon's course. Moreover this Soma makes the dawns (उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)), the times of dawn, of pure birth (शुचिजन्मन (*śucijanmana*)), that is, of pure rising, by its own radiance.
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—as the indicator (in the form of the moon)
- अक्तून् (*aktūn*)—of the dark fortnights and the like

O Indra, in former times the gods established this Soma as the indicator, in the form of the moon, for the days. Therefore this Soma made to shine the nights of the dark fortnights and the like, which are without light, and the days and the years. He made the births of the Dawns pure.

This Soma, Indra, (quaffed by you), has lighted up the unlustrous nights, and days and nights, and years : (the gods) of old have established it as the ensign of days, and it has made the dawns generated in light.

This Indra, shining (रुचानो (*rucāno*)) in the form of the Sun, illumines all the worlds that are without light, made dark by gloom. Likewise this Indra pervades the many dawns with ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), that is, with a radiance that is true in nature or that moves everywhere, and thereby removes the darkness in them. Likewise, being the fulfiller of the desires of men, he moves (ईयते (*īyate*)) with horses yoked by praise (ṛta here meaning praise), on a chariot that is well fastened and that obtains wealth worthy of being well proclaimed.
- रुचानः (*rucānaḥ*)—shining in the form of the Sun
- अरुचः (*arucaḥ*)—all the worlds that are without light
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—with his own lustre of the nature of truth
- स्वर्विदा (*svarvidā*)—and rich in wealth, along with the chariot
- चर्षणिप्राः (*carṣaṇiprāḥ*)—as the fulfiller of the desires of all men

This same Indra, shining in the form of the Sun, illumines all the worlds that are without light. This Indra has pervaded the many dawns with his own lustre of the nature of truth. With a chariot that is fastened and rich in wealth, drawn by horses endowed with praise, Indra moves about as the fulfiller of the desires of all men.

This radiant (Indra) has illumed the non-radiant (worlds): he has pervaded many dawns with true lustre: the benefactor of men moves in (a chariot) drawn by horses, harnessed by praise, laden with riches.

O ancient and shining Indra, being praised, you should quickly bestow (पिन्व (*pinva*), meaning sprinkle, give) many foods on the praiser, one to whom riches are to be given by you. Moreover, to the worshipper, the praiser, give the waters in the form of rain, the plants such as rice, the trees such as mango and jackfruit, which are free of poison or protective, and cows, horses and men who do work.⟨NOTE:32⟩
notes: ನೃನ್ is glossed ಪುತ್ರಭೃತ್ಯಾದಿಗಳನ್ನೂ "sons, servants and the like" in the Kannada, but Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit says men who do work (ಕರ್ಮಕರ್ಮಾನ್ as printed)

en: - गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—you who are to be praised
- वसुदेयाय (*vasudeyāya*)—to him to whom wealth is to be given

O Indra, ancient and shining, you who are to be praised, quickly provide many kinds of food to the praiser, to whom you are to give wealth. To your worshipper provide rain-waters, rice and the like, trees free of poison, cows, horses, and sons, servants and the like.
Sovereign of old, when glorified, you bestow upon him who praises you, and to whom affluence is due, abundant food: grant to the worshipper water, plants, innocuous woods, cattle, horses, and men.

O Indra, drink that Soma which has been pressed for you for your exhilaration. Since the Soma is to be drunk by you, for that reason make your two horses, who are your friends or bear the same name, stand still (अव स्य (*ava sya*)), and afterwards unyoke them from the chariot.
And also, sitting down facing us in this company of us Soma-pressers, sing (प्र गाय (*pra gāya*)), that is, listen to the hymn made by us. Then give food to the sacrificer who praises.
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—the Soma juice that has been pressed, that

O Indra, drink the Soma that has been pressed for you, to cause you delight. Make your friendly horses stand. Afterwards unyoke them, and, sitting in our company facing us, graciously accept our praise. Afterwards give food to the praiser, the sacrificer.
Drink, Indra, (the Soma) that is effused for your exhilaration : stop your friendly steeds: let them loose: sitting in our society, respond to our hymns: give food to him who lauds and worships you.

In the second night-round this Ṛk अस्य पिबेति (*asya pibeti*) is the śastra-yājyā of the Acchāvāka. It is stated in the sūtra: अस्य पिबेति याज्या (*asya pibeti yājyā*) (Ā. Sū. 6-4). O Indra, drink this Soma. O mighty one, being born, you drank in former times that Soma, for exhilaration and for the deed of valour, such as the slaying of Vṛtra. Just this Soma, the cow products such as milk used for cooking, the leaders, the Adhvaryu priests, the waters called Vasatīvarī, and the pressing stones, all these have brought together for this Indra, for your drinking.
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—as soon as you were born
