- क्रत्वे (*kratve*)—and for the deed such as the slaying of Vṛtra
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the milk and the like produced from cows
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the Vasatīvarī waters and the like
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this one in the form of Indra

O great Indra, as soon as you were born, you drank the Soma for your delight and for the deed such as the slaying of Vṛtra: drink that same Soma. The milk and the like produced from cows, the Adhvaryus, the Vasatīvarī waters and the like, and the pressing stones brought together and pressed that same Soma for your drinking, you who are Indra.

Drink, Indra, of this (libation), of which you, mighty one, have drunk as soon as born, for excitement to (great) deeds; that Soma juice which the cows, the priests, the waters, the stones, combine to prepare for your drinking.

In the second night-round, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this Ṛk अस्य पिब (*asya piba*) as the śastra-yājyā mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अस्य पिबेति याज्या (*asya pibeti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

When the fire is kindled and the Soma has been pressed, O Indra, let the horses that are the best carriers bring you here; let them bring you to this sacrifice. And I, with a mind that desires you, invoke you again and again. O Indra, come to our great welfare.
- आ वहंतु (*ā vahaṃtu*)—let them bring to our sacrifice
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come

O Indra, when the fire is kindled and the Soma juice has been pressed, let the horses that are to carry you bring you to our sacrifice. With a mind that desires only your help, I invoke you again and again. O Indra, be gracious for our great welfare.
The fire is kindled ; the Soma, Indra, is effused : let your vigorous horses bring you hither : I invoke you, Indra, with a mind wholly devoted to you: come for our great prosperity.

O Indra, you have gone many times in the past to the sacrifice for the drinking of Soma. For that reason, with a great mind that desires us, come to this our sacrifice, in which the Soma is drunk. Having come, hear these praises of ours that are now being recited. Afterwards may the sacrificer give you food consisting of Soma, for the nourishment of your body.
- ययाथ (*yayātha*)—you have gone to such sacrifices
- सोमपेयं (*somapeyaṃ*)—to our sacrifice, which is ready for the drinking of Soma
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come
- तन्ने (*tanne*)—for the nourishment of the body
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food in the form of Soma

O Indra, you have gone many times in the past to such sacrifices. With a mind that desires our company and is generous, be gracious and come to our sacrifice, which is ready for the drinking of Soma. Hear these praises recited by us. Afterwards may the sacrificer offer you food in the form of Soma, for the nourishment of your body.

You have ever gone (to similar rites): come now with a great mind disposed to drink the Soma: hear these our praises: may the worshipper present to you (sacrificial) food for (the nourishment of) your person.

O Indra, if you are in the far-off region called heaven, or else (ऋधक् (*ṛdhak*), which has the same sense as पृथक् (*pṛthak*)) apart, in another region, or in your own abode, or, what is the use of this specifying, in whatever place you are, then coming from that place, O Girvaṇas, lover of songs, O Indra, accompanied by your horses (नियुतोऽश्वाः (*niyuto 'śvāḥ*)), well pleased together with the Maruts, protect our sacrifice for our protection. Or else: drink our Soma, the means of sacrifice, for your satisfaction.
- स्वे सदने (*sve sadane*)—in your own house
- यत्र वा असि (*yatra vā asi*)—or in whatever region you may be

O Indra, you who accept praise, whether you are in a far-off region, in heaven, or in your own house, in whatever region you may be, come from that region, yoked with horses and joined with the Maruts, and protect our sacrifice, which is the means of our protection.

Whether, Indra, you abide in the distant heaven, in any other place, or in your own abode, or wherever (you may be), from thence do you, who are propitiated by praise, putting to your steeds, protect, together with the Maruts, well pleased, our sacrifice, for our preservation.
O Indra, free from anger, come to our sacrifice, since for you the pressed Soma juices are purified

with the ten-stranded filter. O thunderbolt-bearer, as cows go to their own stall, so the Soma juices go to their own place, such as the Droṇa vessel, facing it (the word to be supplied is: they reach). Therefore, O Indra, you who are the first, the chief, among the gods worthy of sacrifice, come.
- उप याहि (*upa yāhi*)—be gracious and come
- वज्रन् (*vajran*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- गावो न (*gāvo na*)—as cows go with eagerness to their stall
- ओकः (*okaḥ*)—place in the form of the Droṇa vessel
- अच्छ (*accha*)—with eagerness (these Soma juices) go and reach
- यज्ञयानां (*yajñayānāṃ*)—among the gods worthy of sacrifice
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious and come

O Indra, free from anger, be gracious and come to our sacrifice. The Soma juices pressed for you are purified. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, as cows go with eagerness to their stall, the Soma juices reach and fill their own vessel in the form of the Droṇa vessel. O Indra, you who are the chief among the gods worthy of sacrifice, be gracious and come.

Unirascible (Indra), come to the sacrifice : the effused juices are purified for you : they flow, thunderer, (into the pitchers), as cows go to their stalls : come, Indra, the first of those who are to be worshipped.

O Indra, that tongue of yours which has been well fashioned by the creator, which is the most extensive, and with which you drink again and again the essence of the sweet Soma, with that tongue drink our Soma. For that purpose the Adhvaryu, the leader of the rite, having taken the Soma by the hands of the priests, has set out from the place of the oblations to the region of the northern altar. Moreover, O Indra, desiring for yourself the cows belonging to the enemies, let your thunderbolt come together with the enemies; that is, let it kill them.
- ते प्र अस्टात् (*te pra asṭāt*)—stands ready to offer it to you
- सं वर्ततां (*saṃ vartatāṃ*)—let it be hurled against the enemies

O Indra, with that tongue of yours which has been made most excellently and is most extensive, with which you drink the sweet Soma juice many times, drink this Soma juice with that same tongue. The Adhvaryu stands ready to offer it to you. O Indra, let your thunderbolt weapon, desirous of obtaining cows, be hurled against the enemies.

Drink, Indra. with that well-formed and expanded tongue wherewith you ever quaff the juice of the sweet (Soma): before you stands the ministrant priest: let your bolt. Indra. designed (to recover) the cattle, be hurled (against your foes).

notes: the Saṃhitā and Pada blocks of this Ṛk print ॥೨॥

en: This Soma, flowing, showering desires, possessed of forms of many kinds, has been prepared (समकारि (*samakāri*)) for the drinking of Indra, the showerer of desires; it has been refined by pressing and the like. O Indra, lord of the bay horses, stander, presider over all, of mighty strength, drink this Soma, over which you alone are the lord throughout many past days, and which is conceived as your food. The construction is: drink this.
- विश्वरूपः (*viśvarūpaḥ*)—possessed of forms of many kinds
- समकारि (*samakāri*)—has been well refined and made ready
- स्थातः (*sthātaḥ*)—who stand firm as the foremost of all
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—is of the nature of food

This Soma juice, flowing by nature, showering desires, possessed of forms of many kinds, has been well refined and made ready for the drinking of Indra. O Indra, who have horses and stand as the foremost of all, you who are the lord of the Soma juices for many days, drink this Soma, which is of the nature of food for you.

This undropping, omniform Soma, the showerer (of benefits , has been duly prepared for Indra, the showerer (of rain): lord of steeds, ruler over all, mighty (Indra), drink this over which you have of old presided, which is your food.

O Indra, this Soma that has been pressed is better, richer and more praiseworthy than any unpressed Soma of another. Likewise, for you who are knowing and discerning, it is the best and the most delightful: it will give you the greatest delight. O Titirva, Indra, overcomer of the enemies, come to this Soma, the means of sacrifice; come near. And with that Soma fill up all your powers.
- असुतात् (*asutāt*)—than the Soma that has not been pressed
- चिकितुषे (*cikituṣe*)—to you who are fully wise
- तितिर्वः (*titirvaḥ*)—O Indra, who cast down the enemies
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—which is the means of sacrifice
- उप याहि (*upa yāhi*)—be gracious and come

O Indra, this Soma that has been pressed and made ready is better than the Soma that has not been pressed. It is better for causing delight to you who are fully wise. O Indra, who cast the enemies down, be gracious and come to the place where this Soma, the means of sacrifice, is. With this same Soma fill up all your powers.

The effuscd Soma, Indra, is more excellent than that which is not effused : it is better (qualified) to give pleasure to you, who are capable of judging : overcomer (of enemies), approach this sacrifice, and thereby perfect all yours powers.
O Indra, we invoke you; therefore, facing us, come. And our Soma, for your body,

may be sufficient; that is, let it satisfy your body as it desires. And you, O Śatakratu, Indra, doer of many kinds of deeds, delight yourself in our Soma that has been pressed; be satisfied. Thereafter protect us well in the battles. Not only in the battles, but protect us among all the peoples.
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come
- तन्ने (*tanne*)—for the nourishment of the body
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, doer of many deeds
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—in these Somas that have been pressed

O Indra, we invoke you with prayer. Be gracious and come facing us. Let this Soma be sufficient for the nourishment of your body. O Indra, doer of many deeds, find satisfaction in these Somas that have been pressed and made ready. Protect us completely in the battles. Protect us also among all the peoples.
We invoke you, Indra, come down : may the Soma be sufficient for (the satisfaction of) your person: exalt Shatakaratu with the libations, defend us in combats, and against the people.

O Adhvaryu, bring forward to this Indra; that is, offer him the Soma. To what kind of Indra? To him who wishes to drink; to him who knows all things that are to be known; to him whose going is sufficient, who goes readily to the sacrifices, who goes in front of all and never behind, the leader of the sacrifices.
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all that is to be known
- जग्मये (*jagmaye*)—who goes readily to the sacrifices
- अपश्चाद्दघ्वने (*apaścāddaghvane*)—who goes in front of all

O Adhvaryu, offer the Soma to this Indra, who wishes to drink, who knows all that is to be known, whose going is complete, who goes readily to the sacrifices, who goes in front of all, and who is the leader.

Offer, (priests), the libation to him who is desirous to drink ; who knows all things; whose movements are all-sufficient; who goes readily (to sacrifices); the leader (of holy rites), following no one.

In the third (round), in the Svarasāman Niṣkevalya, the triplet beginning एमेनमिति (*emenamiti*) is the stotriya.⟨NOTE:34⟩ It is stated in the sūtra: एमेनं प्रत्येतनेत्याद्यो ना सर्वेषां (*emenaṃ pratyetanetyādyo nā sarveṣāṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-5). O Adhvaryus, go towards this Indra, who is the greatest drinker of Soma, with the Somas as the means. The particle ईं (*īṃ*) has no meaning. What kind of Indra? One who is possessed of ṛjīṣa with the Soma vessels (अमत्रेभिः (*amatrebhiḥ*)), the cups, ladles and the like. Ṛjīṣa is the strength that gathers from the enemies; he possesses it.⟨NOTE:35⟩ Or else, ṛjīṣiṇam is to be connected with what follows: he is possessed of ṛjīṣa with the pressed Somas (इंदुभिः (*iṃdubhiḥ*)); Soma whose essence is gone is ṛjīṣa, and he possesses it. Or else, अमत्रेभिः (*amatrebhiḥ*) means with immeasurable pressed Somas; he is connected with them, that is, united. The construction is: go to an Indra of this kind. Another says: go to this mighty Indra with the Somas that have been pressed and put into the cups, the ladles and the like.
notes: ತೃತೀಯೇ ಸ್ವರಸಾಮಿ ನಿಷ್ಕೇವಲ್ಯ: the words look damaged; the sūtra as printed reads ಏಮೇನಂ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇತನೇತ್ಯಾದ್ಯೋ ನಾ ಸರ್ವೇಷಾಂ with ನಾ doubtful
ಯುಜೀಷಿಣಂ and ಋಜೀಷಿಣಂ both occur in the bhāṣya; the Saṃhitā has ಋಜೀಷಿಣಂ

en: - सोमपातमं (*somapātamaṃ*)—who drinks Soma to the utmost
- आ प्रत्येतन (*ā pratyetana*)—go forth to meet and welcome
- ऋजीषिणं (*ṛjīṣiṇaṃ*)—who has the strength that destroys enemies
- अमत्रेभिः (*amatrebhiḥ*)—that are in the camasa vessel

O Adhvaryus, go forth to meet Indra, who drinks Soma to the utmost, together with the Soma juices. With the Soma juices that have been pressed and that stand in the camasa vessel, meet Indra, who has the strength that destroys enemies.
Proceed to the presence of that deep quaffer of the Soma, with the
Soma juices; to the vigorous Indra with vessels (filled) with the effused

In the Iṣṭi called the third Svara-sāman, in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, the tṛca beginning एमेनं (*emenaṃ*) is to be recited as the Stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, एमेनं प्रत्येतनेत्याद्यो वा सर्वॆषां (*emenaṃ pratyetanetyādyo vā sarvèṣāṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-5).

Sāyaṇa addresses the Adhvaryus: if you go towards Indra with the Somas that are pressed and इंदुभिः (*iṃdubhiḥ*), that is, flowing or shining, then the sense of प्रतिभूषथ (*pratibhūṣatha*) is that you approach Indra; भू (*bhū*) is used in the sense of obtaining.

Then Indra, the मेधिरः (*medhiraḥ*), is wise; or मेधो (*medho*) is the sacrifice and he is its possessor. That Indra knows all your desire; knowing it, and being the assailant of enemies, he brings about each and every desire, that is, he makes you obtain it.
- प्रति भूषथ (*prati bhūṣatha*)—you go to meet him (then)
- आ ईषते (*ā īṣate*)—he makes you obtain
O Adhvaryus, when you go to meet Indra with the pressed and flowing Soma juices, then the wise Indra knows all your desires. And, being the destroyer of enemies, he makes you obtain all your desires.
When, with the effused and flowing Soma juices, you come into his presence, the sagacious (Indra) knows your wish, and the suppressor (of enemies) assuredly grants it, whatever it may be.

अस्मा अस्मा इत् (*asmā asmā it*) means: to this Indra alone, not to another. O Adhvaryu, offer, that is, bestow, the pressed juice of the food called Soma. And may that Indra protect us again and again from the harm done by every enemy who is to be conquered and who is eager and violent.
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the food in the form of Soma
- अस्माअस्मा इत् (*asmāasmā it*)—to Indra alone, and to no other deity
- प्र भर (*pra bhara*)—offer in the best manner (may this same Indra)
- शर्धतः (*śardhataḥ*)—and who is violent; the enemy

O Adhvaryu, offer in the best manner the pressed juice in the form of Soma to Indra alone, and not to any other deity. May this same Indra protect us many times by destroying every enemy who is to be conquered and who is violent.
Offer, priest, to him, and him (only) this libation of (sacrificial)
food, and may he ever defend us against the malignity of every superable

O Indra, in the exhilaration produced by drinking which Soma you destroyed the asura Śambara for King Divodāsa, or, as he also says, you subdued him; Yāska says रध्यतिर्वशगमने (*radhyatirvaśagamane*) (Ni. 6-32). त्यत् (*tyat*) is an adverb of the action: you destroyed in that well-known manner. O Indra, this very Soma has been pressed for you; therefore drink it.
- यस्य मदे (*yasya made*)—satisfied by drinking which Soma juice
- सः आयं सोमः (*saḥ āyaṃ somaḥ*)—that same Soma juice
O Indra, satisfied by drinking which Soma juice you destroyed the asura Śambara for the king named Divodāsa, that same well-known Soma juice has been pressed for you. Drink it.
This Soma, in the exhilaration of which it is known that you have subdued Sambara for (the sake of) Divodasa, is poured out, Indra, for you; drink.

O Indra, you protect the portion of which Soma, the तीव्रसुतं (*tīvrasutaṃ*), that is, the one whose pressing is sharp, belonging to the morning pressing; that intoxicating Soma juice; the मध्यं (*madhyaṃ*), belonging to the midday pressing; and the अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*), belonging to the third pressing. This Soma has been pressed for you; drink it.
- यस्य (*yasya*)—in the portion of which Soma juice
- तीव्रसुतं (*tīvrasutaṃ*)—pressed at the morning pressing and strong
- अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*)—pressed at the third pressing; which Soma juices
- स अयं सोमः (*sa ayaṃ somaḥ*)—that same Soma
- ते सुतः (*te sutaḥ*)—has been pressed for you

O Indra, drink all the several Soma juices there are: the intoxicating one, the one pressed and made ready at the morning pressing, the one pressed at the midday pressing, and the one pressed at the third pressing.
This Soma, the exhilarating draught of which, when fresh effused (at dawn), or at noon, or at the last (or evening worship), you cherish is poured out, Indra, for you: drink.

When the Soma, the intoxicating juice, has been drunk, you released the cows that had been carried off by the Paṇis, which lay inside the mountain made by the asura Vala, firm and tightly shut in. The rest, स सोम इत्यादि गतं (*sa soma ityādi gataṃ*), has been explained already.⟨NOTE:36⟩
notes: ದೃಢಸಿಧಾನಾಶ್ಚ ... ವಲಸ್ಯ ಬಂಧನಾದ್ವಸ್ಯೃಜಃ: the machine-read Sanskrit is damaged; the Gist gives only what is clear

en: - अयं स सोमः (*ayaṃ sa somaḥ*)—that same Soma
O Indra, by the satisfaction of which Soma-drinking you released the cows although they were firmly bound in the middle of the mountain, that same Soma has been pressed for you. Drink it.
This Soma, in the exhilaration of which you have liberated the cattle, firm (fastened) within the rock, is poured out, Indra, for you: drink.

O Indra, you are gladdened by drinking the Soma-food, and so you bear the strength शवः (*śavaḥ*) that belongs to Maghavan, Indra's own and uncommon might. By which Soma your Indra-hood came about. That same Soma has been pressed; drink it.
- अंधस्य (*aṃdhasya*)—by the drinking of the Soma juice
- सः आयं सोमः (*saḥ āyaṃ somaḥ*)—that same Soma
O Indra, by drinking which Soma juice you became glad and obtained the lordship called "Maghavā" and possess uncommon strength, that same Soma has been pressed for you. Drink it.
This Soma, exhilarated (by drinking) of which (sacrificial) food you possess the might of Maghavan, is poured out, Indra, for you : drink.

O wealthy Indra, the Soma that is exceedingly rich, and that with its shining glories is exceedingly glorious: O lord of Svadhā, protector of the Soma-food, that Soma, being pressed, is exhilarating for you.
- स्वधापते (*svadhāpate*)—O protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā

O wealthy Indra, protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā, the Soma that is exceedingly rich, and that by its splendours is exceedingly radiant and glorious, that same Soma, being pressed, is a cause of joy to you.
Opulent Indra, the Soma that abounds with riches, and is most
resplendent with glories, is poured out: is is your exhilaration, Indra,

O Indra of much happiness, that Soma of yours which is the maker of happiness, and which is the giver of wealth to the praisers, to the singers of hymns, that Soma, O lord of Svadhā, being pressed, is exhilarating for you.
- तुविशग्म (*tuviśagma*)—O you who have happiness of many kinds
- स्वधापते (*svadhāpate*)—O protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā

O Indra, who have happiness of many kinds and are the protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā, the Soma that is productive of happiness and gives wealth to your praisers, that same Soma, being pressed, is a cause of joy to you.
The Soma, possessor of felicity, which gives you delight, and which
is the bestower of riches on your votaries, is poured out : it is your
exhilaration, Indra, lord of the offering.

The two words न (*na*) have the sense of conjunction. By drinking which Soma you become both grown and strong, and together with your own helpers, your own Maruts, with strength, you become the destroyer of enemies. That Soma, and so on, as before.
- स्वधापते (*svadhāpate*)—O protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā
- वृद्यो न (*vṛdyo na*)—you grow to full strength
- तुरः (*turaḥ*)—you become the destroyer of enemies

O Indra, protector of the Soma in the form of Svadhā, by drinking which Soma juice you grow to full strength and, joined with your companions the Maruts and with strength, become the destroyer of enemies, that same Soma, being pressed, is a cause of joy to you.
The Soma, whereby you are augmented in strength, and together with your defenders (the Maruts), are victorious (over your foes), is poured out: it is your exhilaration, Indra, lord of the offering.

On the fourth day of the Pṛṣṭha-ṣaḍaha, in the Praüga-śastra, the tṛca त्यमु व (*tyamu va*) is addressed to Indra. It is laid down in the sūtra: त्यमु वो अप्रहणमप त्यं वृजिनं रिपुं (*tyamu vo aprahaṇamapa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ ripuṃ*) (Ā. 7-11). O Ṛtvijs and sacrificers, for you I praise that very Indra. Or else: you praise him. What kind of Indra? अप्रहणं (*aprahaṇaṃ*), one who does not strike, the favourer of his devotees; the lord पतिं (*patiṃ*) and protector of strength; विश्वासाहं (*viśvāsāhaṃ*), the conqueror of every enemy; नरं (*naraṃ*), the leader; मंहिष्ठं (*maṃhiṣṭhaṃ*), the most generous giver; विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*), the beholder of everything.
- (O Ṛtvijs and sacrificers) अप्रहणं (*aprahaṇaṃ*)—who favours his devotees without harming them
- विश्वचर्षणिं (*viśvacarṣaṇiṃ*)—who has the power to see everything
O Ṛtvijs and sacrificers, for your welfare I praise that same Indra, who favours his devotees without harming them, who is the leader and the generous giver, and who has the power to see everything.
(Worshippers), for you I glorify that Indra who disappoints not
(his adorers); the lord of strength, the all-subduing, the leader (of rites),
the most beautiful, the beholder of the universe.

On the fourth day of the sacrifice called Pṛṣṭha-ṣaḍaha, when the Praüga-śastra mantras are recited, the three Ṛks beginning त्र्यमुवः (*tryamuvaḥ*) are to be recited as the tṛca addressed to the deity Indra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, त्यमु वो अप्रहणमप त्यं वृजिनं रिपुं (*tyamu vo aprahaṇamapa tyaṃ vṛjinaṃ ripuṃ*) (Ā. 7-11).

The hymns of praise increase that very strength शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*), the strength that belongs to Indra. Of what kind is he? He is the lord, the master, of whom? Of the harming enemy and of his wealth राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*); that is, he is the taker away of the wealth of enemies. That very drying, consuming strength of this Indra the two divine, shining ones, heaven and earth, quickly attend upon, that is, serve.
- अस्य तं इत् तुष्मं (*asya taṃ it tuṣmaṃ*)—of that Indra, that same strength
The strength of that Indra, the lord of the wealth of the harming enemy, which the hymns of praise cause to grow, that same strength of that Indra the divine heaven and earth quickly worship.
The divine heaven and earth adore that vigour of his, which our
hymns augment, the appropriator of the riches of the foe.

O praisers, the greatness बर्हणा (*barhaṇā*), that is, the abundance and majesty, of your uttered praise is to be spread out for Indra, to be extended for him, so that Indra may know the majesty of the praise. His protections ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*) are like the wise ones विपः (*vipaḥ*), that is, skilled in every work. Or else: the word न (*na*) is a mere filler, and विपः (*vipaḥ*) is to be connected with the wise Indra, of whom the protections are meant. In whom the united, gathered protections arise and appear, for that Indra the praise is to be spread.
- विपो न (*vipo na*)—are, like the wise, competent for all works
- वि रोहंति (*vi rohaṃti*)—arise; for such an
- उपस्तृणीषणि (*upastṛṇīṣaṇi*)—may be extended and made to grow

O praisers, for such an Indra, whose protections, like the wise, are competent for all works, and in whom the protections contained in him arise, may that same greatness of your praise be extended and made to grow.
(Worshippers), the efficacy of your eulogy is to be manifested to that
Indra, whose protections. iike (those) of a sensible man. are displayed as

That Indra knows the दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*), the sacrificer who is competent in rites or who is grown great. Of what kind is Indra? A friend, नवीयान् (*navīyān*), newer, that is, more auspicious or more praiseworthy. And he, drinking the Soma, accumulates, that is, gives, for the gods, the praisers, the best wealth वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*). Moreover he is ससवान् (*sasavān*): सस (*sasa*) is a name for food, so he is provided with the food in the form of the oblation. That Indra, joined with the stout, grown mares that cause shaking, or with Maruts of such a kind, comes with desire to protect the praisers, his friends, and becomes their protector. Or else: ससवान् (*sasavān*) means partaking; it is connected with the stout and shaking ones.
- (Indra) दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—the sacrificer who is competent in rites
- उरुष्या (*uruṣyā*)—coming with the desire to help
notes: ಅಶ್ವಗಳೊಡನೆ "with horses" in the Kannada; Sāyaṇa has vaḍavābhiḥ "with mares" or Maruts

en: Indra knows who the sacrificer is that is competent in rites. Indra, who is a friend to all and worshipful, gives, drinking Soma, the best wealth to the praisers. Indra, provided with food, joined with growing horses, comes with the desire to help the praisers and becomes their protector.
Indra appreciates him who is skilled (in holy rites): a recent friend,
quaffing (the libation), he heaps excellent (wealth) upon the devout :
partaking of (the sacrificial) food, (and brought) by his robust agitators
(of the earth, his steeds), he, through his benevolence, is a protector to

On the path of the sacrifice the Soma, the वेधा (*vedhā*), the arranger and beholder of all, has been drunk by Indra. Or else: Indra, the arranger, has been made to drink, that is, let him drink the Soma. The sentence is explained by a change of form. In that Soma, to resort to it, the gods, that is, the praisers and priests, have made Indra's minds, that is, they perform the rites. And that Indra, so named because he humbles enemies,

bearing his own great body वपुः (*vapuḥ*), being adorable and to be resorted to by praises, may he uncover, that is, make manifest his favourable splendour, for the sake of being seen; the word "splendour" is to be supplied. Or else: वेन्यः (*venyaḥ*) is a form of the root वेनति (*venati*), which means to shine and to desire, and वपुः (*vapuḥ*) is a name for form: Indra, the desirable, being praised with words, may uncover his radiant form, for the sake of being seen.

May Indra, the all-seeing⟨NOTE:39⟩, drink the Soma on the path of the sacrifice. The praisers perform the rite to gladden the mind of Indra. Possessing a body that brings enemies down and is great, and worshipped by praises, may Indra shine forth and appear, so as to be visible to all.
notes: ಸರ್ವ ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾದ in the Bhāvārtha, but ಸರ್ವದ್ರಷ್ಟೃವಾದ (ಸೃಷ್ಟೃವಾದ) in the Pratipadārtha: reading unclear

en: The Soma, creator (of all), on the path of sacrifice, has been drunk:
the worshippers have presented it to gratify the mind (of Indra): may he,
the humilator (of his foes), possessing a vast body, propitiated by our
praises, become manifest to our view.

O Indra, place in us the most brilliant strength दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*). Keep off, hold back, the many hostile armies of us the praisers. Moreover make our food वयः (*vayaḥ*) more abundant by your own wisdom शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*). And in the winning of wealth, lead us, that is, make us go. Or else: protect us for the sharing in wealth.
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—to us who are engaged in rites⟨NOTE:40⟩
notes: ಕರ್ಮದೊಡಗೂಡಿರುವ ನಮಗೆ in the Kannada; Sāyaṇa has ātmīyābhiḥ prajñābhiḥ "by your own wisdom"

en: O Indra, give us the most brilliant strength. Destroy the many hostile armies for us the praisers. Make the best food for us who are engaged in rites. Protect us so that we obtain wealth.
Bestow upon us most brilliant vigour : oppose the numerous enemies
of your worshippers: grant us, for our pious acts, abundant food : secure
us in the enjoyment of wealth.

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, to you the giver of desires, to you alone we have become subordinate. Or else: for you alone we have become engaged in giving oblations. O lord of bay horses, for this reason do not be without desire; desire us always; the root वेनति (*venati*) has the sense of shining and desiring. Among mortals, among men, no other kinsman than you is seen at all. What use is this particular statement? O dear Indra, the ancients call you the impeller रध्रचोदनं (*radhracodanaṃ*) of prosperous, abundant wealth.
- मा वि वेनः (*mā vi venaḥ*)—do not forget us
- नकिः ददृशे (*nakiḥ dadṛśe*)—no one has been seen

O wealthy Indra, we are ready for your service alone, you who grant desires. O Indra, possessor of horses, do not forget us. Other than you, we have seen no kinsman among men. O Indra, everyone has praised you alone as the impeller of wealth and the giver of wealth.

Indra, possessor of affluence, we have recourse to you, the bountiful lord of steeds, be not unfavourable to us: no other kinsman is beheld (by us) amongst men: why else have they called you the bestower of wealth?

notes: no Ṛk number is printed after the Saṃhitā verse; the Pada ends with "೧" (garbled), numbered 11 here as the next in order

en: O Vṛṣabha, showerer of desires, Indra, do not give us up to the destroyer जस्वने (*jasvane*); the root जसि (*jasi*) has the sense of destroying; that is, to a destroyer such as a Rākṣasa. Being in the friendship of you, the wealthy, may we not be harmed. O Indra, your many hindrances, that is, restraints, are set among the enemy people. Or else: the hindrances are ropes for restraining, and many of them are found among your enemy people. For this reason slay those who do not press the Soma and uproot those who do not give oblations.⟨NOTE:42⟩
notes: ಅಸುಷ್ಟೀನನಭಿಷೋತ್ಥನಯಜಮಾನಾನ್: machine-read Sanskrit damaged; rendered as "those who do not press the Soma"

en: - मा ररीथाः (*mā rarīthāḥ*)—do not give up
- मा रिषाम (*mā riṣāma*)—do not let us be harmed
- असुष्टीन् (*asuṣṭīn*)—those who do not press the Soma
- अपृणितः (*apṛṇitaḥ*)—those who do not offer oblations

O Indra, showerer of desires, do not give us up to the harming enemy. Do not let us, who are in the friendship of you, the wealthy, be harmed. O Indra, many hindrances of yours are among the enemy people. Destroy those who do not press the Soma and those who do not offer oblations.

Give us not up, showerer (of benefits), to the obstructor (of our rites) : relying upon the friendship of you, lord of riches, may we be unharmed : many are the hindrances (opposed) to you amongst men: slay those who make no libations, root out those who present no offering.

Like thundering Parjanya who raises up the clouds, Indra raises up and sends forth riches, both of horses and of cattle, in order to give them to the worshippers. The second half of the verse is addressed directly: O Indra, ancient one, you are the upholder of the कारूणां (*kārūṇāṃ*), the praisers. Such as you are, let the wealthy, the niggardly ones who offer no oblations, not harm you. Or else there is a change of number, and the construction is: let them not harm you, the wealthy one.
- अभ्राणीव (*abhrāṇīva*)—as he scatters the clouds in masses upwards (disperses them)
- कारुधायाः (*kārudhāyāḥ*)—as the upholder of the praisers
- मा आ धभन् (*mā ā dhabhan*)—let them not harm

As the thundering Parjanya scatters the clouds upwards in masses (disperses them), Indra spreads out abundantly riches full of horses and full of cattle. O Indra, you yourself, the ancient one, are the upholder of the praisers. Let the niggardly ones, who though wealthy offer no oblations, not harm such a one as you.

As Indra, when thundering, raises the clouds, so he (heaps upon his worshippers) riches of horses and cattle: you, Indra, are the ancient upholder of the sacrificer : let not the opulent wrong you, not presenting (oblations).

O hero, O priest who sends forth the oblations in a special manner: offer the pressed Soma to the great Indra. For that Indra is the lord of this Soma, he who grows strong through the hymns of the praising sages, hymns of both kinds, made in the former time and now being made. Because Indra is the lord of the Soma, Soma is to be given to him; this is the meaning.

Indra, who grows strong through hymns that are of the ancient time and also of the modern time, made by the praising sages, that same Indra is the lord of this Soma. Therefore, O Adhvaryu who offers the oblation, offer the pressed Somas to the exalted Indra.
Ministrant priests offer libations to the mighty Indra, for he is their king, he who has been exalted by the ancient and recent hymns of adoring sages.

In the first night-session this verse, beginning अस्य मदे (*asya made*), is the śastra-yājyā of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest. It is also stated in the sūtra: "अस्य मदे पुरु वर्षांसि विद्वानिति याज्या (*asya made puru varṣāṃsi vidvāniti yājyā*)", Ā. 6-4. When the exhilaration arises from drinking this Soma, the knowing Indra, himself unopposed by others, slew many enemies, the obstructors. Or else: वर्प (*varpa*) is a name for form; knowing the many forms created by the magic of the Asuras, Indra slew the obstructors, the Rakṣas and others, that none before had overcome. Offer that same sweet Soma into the fire for this hero, the fair-jawed one, the one who makes the enemies tremble, to drink it. The address is to the Adhvaryu: offer it.
- वर्षांसि (*varṣāṃsi*)—and of the form of obstructors
- प्र होषि (*pra hoṣi*)—offer in the form of an oblation

When exhilaration arose from drinking this Soma, the wise Indra, unopposed, slew the enemies, who were many in number and of the form of obstructors. To this Indra, who has an excellent jaw and is valiant, offer in the form of an oblation the Soma, which is endowed with sweetness and famed, so that he may drink it.
In the exhilaration of this Soma, the wise Indra, irresistible, has destroyed numerous opposing enemies : offer the sweet-flavoured beverage to that hero. the handsome-chinned, to drink.

In the first night-session the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite this Ṛk beginning अस्य मदे (*asya made*) as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, "अस्य मदे पुरु वर्षांसि विद्वानिति याज्या (*asya made puru varṣāṃsi vidvāniti yājyā*)" (Ā. 6-4).

In the second night-session this verse, beginning पाता सुतं (*pātā sutaṃ*), is the śastra-yājyā of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest alone. It is also stated in the sūtra: "पाता सुतमिंद्रो अस्तु सोमं हंता वृत्रमिति याज्या (*pātā sutamiṃdro astu somaṃ haṃtā vṛtramiti yājyā*)", Ā. 6-4. May this Indra be a good drinker of the pressed Soma. And, exhilarated by that Soma, may he be the slayer, with the thunderbolt, his weapon, of Vṛtra, the obstructing enemy. For both purposes, may he come to our sacrifice even from a far-off place; the meaning is: though staying far away, let him come quickly to our sacrifice to drink Soma. What kind of Indra? The one who is the dwelling-giver of all, the protector of the rites of the thinkers and praisers, the upholder of the doers, the sacrificers.
- पाता अस्तु (*pātā astu*)—let him be the drinker
- कारुधायाः (*kārudhāyāḥ*)—and the upholder of the sacrificers, Indra
- परावतश्चित् (*parāvataścit*)—even though in a very distant place
- गंता (*gaṃtā*)—let him be the one who comes,

Let Indra be the drinker of the pressed Soma. Satisfied by it, let him be the destroyer of the enemy with the thunderbolt. Let Indra, the dweller-giver of all, the protector of the praisers and the upholder of the sacrificers, be one who comes facing our sacrifice, even though he is in a very distant place.

May Indra be the drinker of this effused Soma juice, and exhilarated by it, become the destroyer of Vritra by the thunderbolt: may he come, although from afar, to our sacrifice, (he who is) the giver of dwellings, the upholder of the celebrator (of religious rites).

In the second night-session the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite this Ṛk beginning पाता सुतं (*pātā sutaṃ*) as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, "पाता सुतमिंद्रो अस्तु सोमं हंता वृत्रमिति याज्या (*pātā sutamiṃdro astu somaṃ haṃtā vṛtramiti yājyā*)" (Ā. 6-4).

In the third night-session this verse, beginning इदं त्यत् (*idaṃ tyat*), is the śastra-yājyā of the Praśāstṛ priest. It is also stated in the sūtra: "इदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिति याज्या (*idaṃ tyatpātramiṃdrapānamiti yājyā*)", Ā. 6-4. The vessel, to be drunk, fit for Indra's drinking, dear and favourable to Indra, this Soma-nature immortal drink, has been drunk; let Indra drink. The passive form stands for the active by a change of voice. Or else: let this immortal drink be drunk by Indra, in such a manner that the Soma is drunk.

सौमनसाय (*saumanasāya*) means for the sake of good-mindedness; Soma is to be drunk in such a manner that it delights the god Indra. Having drunk the Soma, Indra is to remove from us hatred, that is, the hater, and sin.
- सौमनसाय (*saumanasāya*)—for the sake of showing favour
- मत्सत् (*matsat*)—for the very reason that it gladdens
- पात्रं (*pātraṃ*)—that which is fit to be drunk
- इंद्रपानं (*iṃdrapānaṃ*)—that which is fit for Indra to drink
- अपायि (*apāyi*)—let it be drunk (after that, Indra)
- वि युयवत् (*vi yuyavat*)—let him keep far away and separate

In order that Indra may attain the delight of showing us favour, let this ambrosia be drunk, which is fit to be drunk, fit for Indra to drink, agreeable to Indra, famed, and of the nature of Soma. Thereafter let Indra keep our enemies and our sins apart from us (or let him destroy them).

May this ambrosia, the appropriate beverage of Indra, of which he is fond, be quaffed (by him), so that it may inspire the divinity with favourable feelings (towards us), and that he may remove from us our adversaries, and (all) iniquity.

In the third night-session the priest called Praśāstra ⟨NOTE:44⟩ is to recite this Ṛk beginning इदं त्यत् (*idaṃ tyat*) as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, "इदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिति याज्या (*idaṃ tyatpātramiṃdrapānamiti yājyā*)" (Ā. 6-4).
notes: ಪ್ರಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ printed; the bhāṣya has ಪ್ರಶಾಸ್ತುಃ

en: O Maghavan, wealthy one, O hero, valiant Indra, exhilarated by this Soma now at hand, slay the enemies, whether जामिं (*jāmiṃ*), a kinsman, or अजामिं (*ajāmiṃ*), one unlike him; that is, enemies of both kinds, intent on acting against us. Do them harm. Moreover, O Indra, drive back the enemies who are अभिषेणान् (*abhiṣeṇān*), whose armies advance against us, and who आदेदिशानान् (*ādediśānān*) again and again aim and hurl their weapons in our direction. Press them so that they turn their faces away; after that, slay them.
- अभि आदेदिशानान् (*abhi ādediśānān*)—and those who hurl weapons at us, the enemies
- जहि च (*jahi ca*)—and destroy them also

O Indra, wealthy and valiant, gladdened by this Soma, destroy our enemies. Whether that enemy be a kinsman to us or not a kinsman, when he falls upon us and hurls weapons at us, do harm to such enemies so that they run back, and destroy them.
Exhilarated by it, valiant Maghavan, slay our unfriendly adversaries, whether kinsmen or unrelated (to us) : put to flight, Indra, hostile armies menacing us (with their weapons), and slay them.

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, in these battles of ours make for us great wealth, वरिवः (*varivaḥ*), that is easily obtained; स्म (*sma*) is a filler. Moreover, O Indra, for the winning of waters, or of wealth that is to be gained ⟨NOTE:45⟩, of a son and of a grandson, make us, the praisers, अर्धं (*ardhaṃ*), that is, prosperous. Or else: make us the cutters-down of the enemies who are अर्धकारिणः (*ardhakāriṇaḥ*); स्म (*sma*) is the filler.
notes: ಅಪಾಮಾಪ್ತವ್ಯಾನಾಂ ಧನಾನಾಂ ವೋದಕಾನಾಂ ನಾ: the ನಾ looks misread

en: - तोकस्य (*tokasya*)—for the sake of a son
- तनयस्य (*tanayasya*)—for the sake of a grandson

O wealthy Indra, in these battles that have put us into distress, bring about for us wealth that is great and easily obtained. O Indra, to gain victory for the sake of water, for the sake of a son and for the sake of a grandson, make us, the praisers, prosperous.
Affluent Indra, facilitate to us (the acquirement of) vast riches in these our battles: (enable us) to ga n the victory: make us prosperous with rain, and with sons and graudsons.

O Indra, let the horses bring you to drink the Soma, which is the showerer's, that is, gladdening, exhilarating. What kind of horses? They are वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*), showerers of desires; युजानाः (*yujānāḥ*), yoked of themselves to the chariot; वृषरथासः (*vṛṣarathāsaḥ*), those whose chariot is a showerer, one that rains desires; वृषरश्मयः (*vṛṣaraśmayaḥ*), those whose reins are showerers, that is, whose bridles rain; अत्याः (*atyāḥ*), ever moving; अस्मत्रांचः (*asmatrāṃcaḥ*), going towards us; वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*), ever young; वज्रवाहः (*vajravāhaḥ*), bearing weapons such as the thunderbolt; सुयुजः (*suyujaḥ*), well yoked.
- वृषरथासः (*vṛṣarathāsaḥ*)—possessing a chariot that bestows what is wished
- वज्रवाहः (*vajravāhaḥ*)—bearing weapons such as the thunderbolt
- मदाय (*madāya*)—and gladdening, for the drinking of Soma

O Indra, let horses that are showerers of desires, joined to the chariot, possessing a chariot that bestows what is wished, swift-going, coming towards us, possessing youth, bearing weapons such as the thunderbolt, and excellently yoked, bring you for the drinking of Soma, which is rich in wealth and gladdening.

Let your vigorous steeds, harnessed of their own will, drawing your wish-bestowing chariot, guided by shower-yielding reins, quick-moving, hastening towards us, youthful, thunder-bearing, well-yoked, bring you to the bountiful, exhilarating (libations).

O Indra, showerer of desires, your young horses, वृषणः (*vṛṣaṇaḥ*), sprinklers, pouring ghee, that is, water, like waves of the ocean, exult and become glad; they have mounted your द्रोणं (*droṇaṃ*), your chariot made of wood. Therefore, the sense is, come. Why? He says: O Indra, for you, the young, ever youthful bull, the showerer of desires, the Adhvaryus offer forward, carry forward for the oblation, the Soma that is your portion, among the Somas pressed by the showering stones. Therefore come; this is the meaning.
- ऊर्मयो न (*ūrmayo na*)—like the waves of the sea that dance
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the juice allotted to your portion
- प्र भरंति (*pra bharaṃti*)—they offer in the form of oblation

O Indra, showerer of desires, your horses, which are young, pouring forth water and showing gladness like the dancing waves of the sea, stand joined to your chariot. O Indra, for you, who are young and a showerer of desires, the Adhvaryus offer in the form of oblation the juice that belongs to your portion among the Soma juices pressed by crushing with stones.

Showerer (of benefits), your vigorous water-shedding steeds, like the waves (of the sea), exulting, are harnessed to your car ; for they, (the priests , offer to you, the showerer (of benefits), ever youthful, the libation of the Soma juices expressed by the stones.

O Indra, you are the showerer of heaven, दिवः (*divaḥ*): you sprinkle it with oblations. You are the वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) of the earth, the showerer of desires. You are the वृषा (*vṛṣā*) of the rivers, flowing ones, filling them with rain. Likewise you are the showerer of desires of the स्तियानां (*stiyānāṃ*), the beings gathered together, of the nature of the stationary and the moving. Or else: स्तियाः (*stiyāḥ*) are the waters gathered together, and you are the one who showers them. O showerer of desires, Indra, for you, the excellent one, the sprinkler, the sweet juice, flavourful, or praiseworthy, or full of juice, of the nature of juice, to be drunk like honey, इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*), the Soma, swells and grows; therefore, the sense is, come and drink that Soma.
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—as the bestower of what is wished
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—you are the showerer of desires
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you fill the water with rain
- स्तियानां (*stiyānāṃ*)—for all beings that form a collection
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—you are the showerer of desires
- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—O Indra, bestower of what is wished

O Indra, showerer of desires, you are the bestower of what is wished for the heavenly world. For the earth you are the showerer of desires by giving rain. You fill the rivers with water by rain. For all beings that form a collection you are the showerer of desires. O Indra, bestower of what is wished, for you, the excellent and the cause of rain, the Soma juice is ready for drinking.
You, Indra, are the showerer of heaven, the bedewer of earth, the the feeder of the rivers, the supplier of the aggregated (waters): for you,
showerer (of desires), who are the most excellent shedder of rain, the sweet Soma, the honey-flavoured juice, is ready to be quaffed.

On the word स्तियानां (*stiyānāṃ*) Yāska has given this explanation: स्तिया आपो भवंति स्त्यायनात् । वृषा सिंधूनां वृषभः स्तियानां इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*stiyā āpo bhavaṃti styāyanāt | vṛṣā siṃdhūnāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ stiyānāṃ ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-17). स्तियाः (*stiyāḥ*) means water, because the word स्त्यायन (*styāyana*) has the meaning "bring together". When the earth, and the many substances in it, are broken into fine particles and do not cohere, water makes them come together (by pouring water and kneading). Water has the power of making two substances unite. Therefore water has received the name स्तिया (*stiyā*). In this matter the Vedic sentence in the present Ṛk, वृषा सिंधूनां वृषभः स्तियानां (*vṛṣā siṃdhūnāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ stiyānāṃ*), is itself the example; this is the purport of the etymology.

This shining Indu, the Soma, born together with Indra his friend, the yoked one, stopped by his strength the Paṇi, the merchant, the Asura named Vala, who seizes cattle. Or else: he is called Paṇi because he is the lord of the Paṇis. He held that Asura back by strength, restrained him. Moreover, of his own wealth in the form of cattle, the protector, the guardian, of the inauspicious, the one who gives no happiness

The Soma carried off the weapons of Vala, such as the thunderbolt, and carried off his magical powers too. O Indra, by the strength of friendship with you Soma has done all this; who can describe your greatness? This is a praise of Indra.
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—as soon as he was born
- स्वस्य (*svasya*)—of his own wealth in the form of cattle
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—the deceitful powers also (he carried off)
notes: ನಾಶಮಾಡಿದನು "destroyed" in the gloss; Sāyaṇa has ಅಸ್ತಭ್ನಾತ್ ನ್ಯರುಧತ್ "stopped, restrained"

en: This divine Soma, joined with Indra, as soon as he was born destroyed by his own strength the Asura called Paṇi. He carried off the weapons of Vala, the guardian of his own wealth in the form of cattle and the inauspicious one. He carried off his deceitful powers also.
This divine Soma, with Indra for its ally, crushed, as soon as generated, Pani by force: this Soma baffled the devices and the weapons of the malignant secreter of (the stolen wealth, the cattle).

This Soma made the dawns, the times of dawn, सुपत्नीः (*supatnīḥ*), women whose husband and protector is the fair Sūrya; he made them so. He himself placed light, brilliance, within the sun, in the middle of the solar orb. This Soma, in the form of the plant and threefold through the three pressings, found the ambrosia, the immortal drink, the cause of immortality, that lay deeply hidden, unseen, among the gods who shine in heaven and are spread out in the third region. O Indra, the praise of Indra is to be understood thus: Soma has done so by virtue of your help. Or else the word इदं (*idaṃ*) refers to Indra himself: he made the dawns have a fair husband; he placed light within the sun; among the gods shining in heaven, in the three places, this Indra found the Soma, threefold through the three pressings, hidden, covered by the vessels, the cause of deathlessness.
- सुपत्नीः (*supatnīḥ*)—as wives of the excellent Sūrya
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Soma in the form of the plant
- त्रितेषु (*triteṣu*)—and spread out in the third place, among the gods
- त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*)—of three forms in the form of the three pressings
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—and free from death, the juice

This Soma made the dawns to be wives of the excellent Sūrya. This same Soma placed brilliance in the middle of the solar orb. This Soma in the form of the plant obtained the juice, which was hidden among the gods shining in the heavenly world and spread out in the third place, which has three forms in the form of the three pressings, and which is free from death.
This Soma made the dawns happily wedded to the sun : this Soma placed the light within the solar orb: this (Soma) has found the threefold ambrosia hidden in heaven in the three bright regions.

This Soma propped apart heaven and earth, set them each in its place. Moreover, this Soma yoked the chariot of the sun, सप्तरश्मिं (*saptaraśmiṃ*), furnished with seven rays, with seven horses, with seven wheels ⟨NOTE:47⟩. So also this Soma holds within the cows, शच्या (*śacyā*), by his intelligence in the form of resolve, the matured, produced milk, a spring, उत्सं (*utsaṃ*), which flows forth. दशयंत्रं (*daśayaṃtraṃ*) is an epithet of the spring: furnished with ten instruments, the eye, ear and the rest, which are the cause of its flowing forth. This word is explained by another khila mantra: चक्षुश्च श्रोत्रं च मनश्च वाक्च प्राणापानौ देह इदं शरीरं । द्वौ प्रत्यंचावनुलोमौ विसर्गावेतं तं मन्ये दशयंत्रमुत्समिति । (*cakṣuśca śrotraṃ ca manaśca vākca prāṇāpānau deha idaṃ śarīraṃ | dvau pratyaṃcāvanulomau visargāvetaṃ taṃ manye daśayaṃtramutsamiti |*). Or else: this Indra propped apart heaven and earth and set them each in its place; he himself yoked the seven-rayed chariot of the sun; this same Indra holds within the cows, by his own act, the matured milk. For such an Indra, Soma holds the spring-like juice, the flowing one, furnished with ten cups, the Aindravāyava and others, drawn and held in check. At the morning pressing ten cups, the Aindravāyava and the rest, are drawn. And so the Brāhmaṇa says: नव प्रातर्ग्रहा गृह्यंते नवभिर्बहिष्पवमाने स्तुवते स्तुते स्तोमे दशमं गृह्णाति । (*nava prātargrahā gṛhyaṃte navabhirbahiṣpavamāne stuvate stute stome daśamaṃ gṛhṇāti |*), Ai. Brā. 3-1. And elsewhere it is recited: दशैतानध्वर्युः प्रातःसवने ग्रहान् गृह्णातीति (*daśaitānadhvaryuḥ prātaḥsavane grahān gṛhṇātīti*). With this in view the epithet दशयंत्रं (*daśayaṃtraṃ*) is used.
notes: ನವಾಯುನಕ್ after ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರಂ: the reading looks damaged

en: - सप्तरश्मिं (*saptaraśmiṃ*)—as one having seven rays (rays or wheels)
- गोषु अंतः (*goṣu aṃtaḥ*)—in the bodies of the cows
- शच्या (*śacyā*)—by his intelligence in the form of resolve
- दशयंत्रं (*daśayaṃtraṃ*)—that which consists of ten instruments

This Soma set up heaven and earth individually. This same Soma made the chariot of Sūrya one with seven rays. And by his intelligence in the form of resolve he has filled the bodies of the cows with milk that flows forth, consists of ten instruments, and is ripened.
This (Soma) has fixed heaven and earth: this has harnessed the seven-rayed chariot (of the sun): this Soma has developed of its own will the mature deeply-organized secretion in the cows.
The supplementary mantras (pariśiṣṭa) to be recited at the end of this sūkta are given at the end of this Maṇḍala.
The Indra who brought, by good guidance, from a distant place the two kings named Turvaśa and Yadu, who had been thrown into a far country by enemies, may that youthful Indra be our friend.
- यदुं (*yaduṃ*)—and the one named Yadu, the two kings
The Indra who brought the two kings named Turvaśa and Yadu from a very distant country by his excellent guidance, may that same youthful Indra be a friend to us also.
May that youthful Indra, who by good guidance, brought Turvasa and Yadu from afar, (be) our friend.

Even on one who is अविप्रे (*avipre*), not a विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), a praiser, Indra bestows वयः (*vayaḥ*), food; what need to say that he bestows it on the praiser? That Indra, even with a horse that is not swift-going, becomes the winner of the wealth that has been deposited among the enemies.
- अविप्रे चित् (*avipre cit*)—even to a man who is not a praiser
- अनाशुना अर्वता चित् (*anāśunā arvatā cit*)—even though he goes with a horse that does not move swiftly
- जेता (*jetā*)—he brings under his own control
Indra gives food even to a man who is not a praiser. Even when he goes with a horse that does not move swiftly, he brings under his own control the wealth deposited among the enemies.
Indra gives sustenance, even to the undevout : he is the conqueror of wealth accumulated (by enemies), through (going against) them with a slow-paced steed.

The प्रणीतयः (*praṇītayaḥ*) of this Indra, his excellent leadings, his ways of bringing about, are great; and likewise the प्रशस्तयः (*praśastayaḥ*), the excellent praises made by the praisers, are many. And so the ऊतयः (*ūtayaḥ*), the protections of this Indra, do not decay, do not diminish, but always only increase.
- प्रशस्तयः (*praśastayaḥ*)—the acts in the form of praise
- न क्षीयंते (*na kṣīyaṃte*)—do not come to destruction
The excellent and skilful policies of Indra are of the greatest majesty. The ways of praising him are also many. There is no destruction of Indra's protections.
Vast are his designs, manifold are his praises, his protections are never withdrawn,

Friends, fellow praisers, offer worship to Indra, who is to be borne along and reached by the Brahmas, that is, by mantras: recite the śastras. And sing the stotras. For that same Indra is for us great and a प्रमतिः (*pramatiḥ*), an excellent understanding; the meaning is that he is the giver of such understanding.
- ब्रह्मवाहसे (*brahmavāhase*)—to Indra, who is fit to be approached through praise alone
- अर्चत (*arcata*)—worship by reciting the śastra mantras
- प्रमतिः (*pramatiḥ*)—and excellent; he is the giver of intelligence

O praisers, who are friends, recite the śastra mantras and worship Indra, who is fit to be approached through praise alone. Sing with stotras. That same Indra is for us the giver of an intelligence that is great and excellent.
Offer worship and praises, friends, to him who is to be attracted by prayers ; for he verily is our great intelligence.

O Vṛtrahan, Indra, slayer of the Vṛtras, the enemies, you are the protector of one praiser and of two praisers; the meaning is that you are the protector of all praisers. And also of such a person as we are: as we, with sons and grandsons of many kinds, have been protected by you, so you are the protector of such a person too, and no one else is; this is the meaning.
- एकस्य (*ekasya*)—for a praiser who is alone
- द्वयोः (*dvayoḥ*)—and for two praisers who are together
- ईदृते (*īdṛte*)—for people like us also you are protector
O Indra, destroyer of enemies, whether your praiser is alone or two are together, you are the protector of all of them. You are the protector also of devotees like us, your praisers.
Slayer of Vritra, you are the protector of one (adorer), or of two, and of such as we are.

O Indra, you alone lead the haters across and bring us over; उ (*u*) is a mere filler. Likewise you make prosperous us, the praisers who recite the uktha śastras. Since you are called सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*), endowed with good heroes, sons, grandsons and the like, to be given to praisers, and are praised by men, the leaders of the praises, therefore give those same things to us also; this is what is to be supplied. ⟨NOTE:50⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟನತಿ and ಹರ್ಷಿ appear garbled; sense taken as the haters / you make prosperous

en: - अति नयसि (*ati nayasi*)—you drive far away from us
- उक्तशंसिनः (*uktaśaṃsinaḥ*)—those who praise you by reciting the uktha mantras
- सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*)—you who favour with excellent heroic sons and the like

O Indra, it is you who drive far away from us those who hate us. You make prosperous those who praise you by reciting the uktha mantras. You, who favour with excellent heroic sons and the like, are praised by the praisers.
Remove (from us) those who hate us: prosper those who repeat your praise : bestower of excellent male descendants. you are glorified by men.

The great one; one who is borne along by Brahmas, that is, by mantras in the form of praise; a friend, one who has become a friend of ours; ऋग्मियं (*ṛgmiyaṃ*): ṛgmā means ṛcs, and he is worthy of them, that is, worthy of praise. Such an Indra I call with praises, as one calls a cow in order to milk her; I invite him in order to milk out our desires.
- ब्रह्मवाहसं (*brahmavāhasaṃ*)—who is borne along by praise
- यग्नियं (*yagniyaṃ*)—who is worthy of praise: such an Indra
- गां न (*gāṃ na*)—as one milks a cow
- दोहसे (*dohase*)—to milk out the wealth of that Indra
Indra, who is of the form of Brahman, who is borne along by praise, who is a friend and worthy of praise, I entreat and call with praises, to milk wealth from him as milk is drawn from a cow.
I invoke with hymns Indra, our friend, who is Brahma, who is attracted by prayer and entitled to adoration, to milk him as a cow.

वीरस्य (*vīrasya*) means of the powerful one; पृतनासहः (*pṛtanāsahaḥ*): pṛtanās are enemy armies, and he is their overcomer. In whose hands, that is, in the arms of that Indra, all treasures, existing in a twofold way as heavenly and earthly, are found: so the seers say, they declare it constantly. That Indra I call; this is the connection with the previous verse.
- पृतनासहः (*pṛtanāsahaḥ*)—who defeats the armies of enemies
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—that exist in two forms, heaven and earth
- नि ऊचुः (*ni ūcuḥ*)—the seers have praised thus (that Indra I call)
I call with prayer that Indra, valiant and the defeater of the armies of enemies, in whose arms the seers have praised all treasures, existing in the two forms of heaven and earth, as established.
In the hands of whom, the heroic subduer of hostile armies, (the sages) have declared, are all the treasures in both (heaven and earth).

O अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*): adri is the thunderbolt, and Indra is its possessor. O lord of Śacī, Indra, split open the firm things of the people, that is, of the enemies, even their strong and ancient strongholds or powers; split them apart.
That is, uproot them in every way. O unbending one, one who has not bowed, exalted above all, Indra, destroy also the magic devices made by the enemies.
- दृळ्हानि चित् (*dṛḷhāni cit*)—even though extremely hard, their towns
- अनानत (*anānata*)—O Indra, whose power bends to none
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—destroy the deceitful acts of the enemies

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt and lord of Śacī, tear apart the towns of the enemies, even though they are extremely strong. O Indra, whose power bends to none, destroy all the deceitful acts of the enemies.
Wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of Sachi, demolish the strong (cities) of men : (baffle), unbending (Indra), their devices.

O true one, of unfailing nature; O drinker of Soma, worthy to drink Soma; O lord of foods, protector of foods: O Indra, such as you are, we who desire fame, that is, food for ourselves, call upon you alone, that is, we praise you; this is the meaning.
- वाजानां पते (*vājānāṃ pate*)—who is the protector of foods
O Indra, whose nature is truth, who drink Soma and protect foods, we who desire food praise and call upon you, the renowned one.
Veracious Indra, drinker of the Soma, provider of sustenance, we, desirous of food, invoke such as you are.

O Indra, we praise you alone; this is what is to be supplied. You who in former times were to be invoked, that is, became one to be invoked, for the gaining of wealth; and you who, now too, wealth being placed among the enemies as the cause, have become one to be invoked: such as you are, hear our call, our hymn; listen.
- तमु त्वा (*tamu tvā*)—(O Indra) we praise that renowned same you
- हव्यः आसिथ (*havyaḥ āsitha*)—were called for the sake of wealth
- यो वा (*yo vā*)—and who, that same you

O Indra, I praise that renowned Indra. You who were called of old for the sake of wealth, you who even now are called for the gaining of the wealth placed among the enemies, that same you, hear our praise.
(We invoke) you, such as you are, you who have been invocable of old, and who are now to be invoked for the wealth held (by the foe): hear our invocation.

O Indra, we, favoured by you who are pleased with our praises directed to you, may win, with our own horses, the horses of the enemies, their praiseworthy, renowned foods, and the wealth placed among the enemies. By your favour may we conquer.
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—we who are favoured by you
- अर्वद्भिः (*arvadbhiḥ*)—by the strength of our horses
- अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—the horses of the enemies also
O Indra, we, pleased by our praises and favoured by you, can conquer, by the strength of our horses, the horses of the enemies, their praiseworthy foods, and the wealth lying among the enemies.
(Favoured) by you, Indra, (who are propitiated) by our hymns, (we overcome) with our steeds, the steeds (of the enemy), and we conquer abundant food, and the wealth held (by the foe)

O hero, one who sends the enemies far apart in various ways; O गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*), Indra, to be served with songs of praise: wealth placed among the enemies being the occasion, you, grown great, become the victor over the enemies in the battle.
- हिते (*hite*)—that is placed among the enemies
- वितंतसाय्कः (*vitaṃtasāykaḥ*)—as the conqueror of the enemies
O Indra, valiant and worshipped with praises, you who have grown great in the battle fought for the wealth placed among the enemies conquer the enemies.
Heroic and adorable Indra, verily you are mighty in battle, and victor of the wealth held (by the enemy).
O destroyer of enemies, Indra, that course of yours which is exceedingly swift, with that course impel our chariot; send it quickly, for the conquest of the enemies.
O Indra, destroyer of enemies, by that exceedingly swift course which is yours, impel our chariot for the conquest of the enemies.
Destroyer of enemies with that your velocity, which is of exceeding swiftness impel our chariots (against the foe).

O victorious Indra, you who are रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*), exceedingly a charioteer, a great chariot-warrior: with our chariot, which is the attacker and overcomer of enemies, conquer the wealth placed among the enemies; conquer it for our sake.
- रथीतमः (*rathītamaḥ*)—you who have an excellent chariot
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—that is placed among the enemies
O victorious Indra, you who have an excellent chariot, conquer for us, with the chariot that is ours and that defeats the enemies, the wealth placed among the enemies.
Victorious Indra, you are the chief of charioteers ; conquer the wealth that is held (by the enemy) with our assailing car.

विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*): the one who sees everything in a special way; वृषक्रतुः (*vṛṣakratuḥ*): one whose work is rain. That Indra who alone, and no other, was born as the lord, the overlord, of the कृष्णीनां (*kṛṣṇīnāṃ*), the subjects: that very Indra, O praiser, praise.
- विचर्षणिः (*vicarṣaṇiḥ*)—who is able to see everything
- वृषक्रतुः (*vṛṣakratuḥ*)—who has the work of rain
- एक इत् (*eka it*)—as one without a second
O praiser, praise that same Indra who can see everything, who has the work of rain, and who was born as one without a second, as lord of all the subjects.
Praise that Indra who alone has been born the supervisor (of all), the lord of men, the giver of rain.

O Indra, you who by your protection are शिवः (*śivaḥ*), a giver of happiness, and for that very reason a friend: being a friend, you were formerly a kinsman of us who praise, of us the praisers alone. Such as you are, now make us happy.
- गृणतां इत् (*gṛṇatāṃ it*)—only to the praisers
O Indra, you who by your protection are beneficent and a friend, and who have been a kinsman only to the praisers: such as you are, make us happy.
Indra, you have ever been the friend of those who praise you, and the insurer of their happiness by your protection; grant us felicity.

O Indra, possessor of the thunderbolt, hold the thunderbolt, the कुलिशं (*kuliśaṃ*), in your two arms. For what purpose? For the slaying of the Rākṣasas. And having held it, overcome exceedingly the contending, approaching armies of the Asuras.
- वज्रिवः (*vajrivaḥ*)—O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt
- रक्षोहत्याय (*rakṣohatyāya*)—for the destruction of the Rākṣasas
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—the armies of the Asuras that contend
O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt, hold the thunderbolt in both your arms for the destruction of the Rākṣasas. Defeat completely the armies of the Asuras, who contend with you and fall upon you.
Wielder of the thunderbolt, take the bolt in your hands for the destruction of the Rakshasas, and utterly overthrow those who defy you.

Indra is called upon as: ancient, of long standing, the first of all; the one who joins, that is, the giver, of riches; a friend, a companion; the impeller of the कीरि (*kīri*), the praisers; and ब्रह्मवाहस्तमं (*brahmavāhastamaṃ*), he who is most of all to be borne along by the Brahmas, the mantras. Such an Indra I call; I invite him.
- युजं (*yujaṃ*)—who joins them to the praisers
- कीरिचोदनं (*kīricodanaṃ*)—who is the impeller of the praisers
- ब्रह्मवाहस्तमं (*brahmavāhastamaṃ*)—who is most of all to be borne along by mantras; that Indra
I call with praise that Indra who is ancient, who joins riches to the praisers, who is a friend, the impeller of the praisers, and the one who is most of all to be borne along by mantras.
I invoke the ancient Indra, the giver of riches, (our) friend, the encourager of his adorers, who is to be propitiated by prayer.

That same Indra alone rules over all the riches that belong to the earth, and no one else does; the verb पत्यते (*patyate*) has the sense of exercising lordship. What kind of Indra is he? गिर्वणस्तमः (*girvaṇastamaḥ*): he who is most of all to be served with songs of praise; and अध्रिगुः (*adhriguḥ*), one whose going is not struck back, that is, whose course is unobstructed. ⟨NOTE:51⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: "ಅಧಿ ಗುರಧೃತಗಮನಃ" is garbled; sense taken from the following ಅಪ್ರತಿಹತಗತಿ

en: - गिर्वणस्तमः (*girvaṇastamaḥ*)—who is worshipped exceedingly with praises
That same Indra, who is worshipped exceedingly with praises and whose course is unobstructed, is the lord, without a second, of all riches belonging to the earth.
He alone rules over all terrestrial riches, he who is entitled to especial praise. he who is irresistible.

O lord of cattle, protector of cows, fulfil our desire with mares, in such a way that it is धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*), bold, able to destroy poverty. Or else धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*) is an epithet of Indra, meaning the subduer of enemies. ⟨NOTE:52⟩ And fulfil our desire likewise with foods accompanied by many cows and by many horses.
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: "ಧರ್ಷಕಸ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥ॥" garbled; read as meaning "subduer"

en: - धृषत् (*dhṛṣat*)—so that our poverty is destroyed
- अश्विभिः (*aśvibhiḥ*)—and filled with horses: with such riches fulfil our desired objects

O Indra, protector of cattle, with the help of your niyuts, bring about the fulfilment of our desired objects, so that our poverty is destroyed. Fulfil our desired objects with riches that are full of food, full of cows and full of horses.
Lord of cattle, (coming) with your mares, satisfy our desires completely with (abundant) food, with horses, and with cows.

O praisers, when Soma has been pressed, sing together that stotra to Indra, who is called by many sacrificers, who is सत्वने (*satvane*), the subduer of enemies, or the giver of riches; that stotra which is शं (*śaṃ*), a source of comfort, to the mighty Indra, as grass is a source of comfort to a cow; this is the meaning. ⟨NOTE:53⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: "ಶತ್ರುವಾಣಾಂ ಸಾದಯಿತ್ರೇ" garbled; read as "of enemies"

en: - गवे न (*gave na*)—as grass is a means of comfort to cattle
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma juice has been pressed
- पुरुहूताय (*puruhūtāya*)—to him who is called by many
- सत्वने (*satvane*)—and is the giver of wealth, Indra
- गाय (*gāya*)—recite in the form of song

O praisers, gathered together, when the Soma juice has been pressed, recite in the form of song, to Indra, who is called by many and is the giver of wealth, such a praise as becomes a source of comfort to the mighty Indra, as grass is to cattle.
Sing praises, when your libation is poured out, to him who is the invoked of many, the subduer (of foes), giving him gratification, like (fresh pasture) to cattle.

वसुः (*vasuḥ*) is the one who causes to dwell: that Indra does not withhold, न घ (*na gha*), indeed not, the gift of food, of strength, accompanied by many cows; he does not restrain it, does not bring it to a stop, if he should hear these praises of ours. The meaning is that whenever he hears the stotra he always gives.
- न घ नि यमते (*na gha ni yamate*)—he certainly does not withhold
When Indra, the giver of dwellings, certainly hears our praises, then he certainly does not withhold the gift of food filled with cattle.
The giver of dwellings verily withholds not the gift of food conjoined with cattle, when he hears our praises.

कुवित्सस्य (*kuvitsasya*): Kuvitsa is the name of someone; Indra, the destroyer of the Dasyus, goes forth to that one's own cow-pen, the cattle-shed full of many cows; he goes forth vigorously. Since this is so, he uncovers for us, by his own acts or by his wisdom, those hidden cows. ⟨NOTE:54⟩
notes: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ: the explanation of ಕುವಿತ್ಸಸ್ಯ and "ದಸ್ಯೂನಾಮುಪಕ್ಷಪಯಿತ್ಯಣಾಂ" are garbled

en: - अप वरत् (*apa varat*)—he keeps (the door) opened

Indra, the destroyer of enemies, easily enters the cow-pen, filled with cows, of the Asura named Kuvitsa. For that very reason, by his excellent acts, he keeps the door of that cow-house opened for us also.
Then the destroyer of the Dasyus, proceeds to the cattle-crowded folds of Kuvitsa, and by his acts opens them for us.

O Śatakratu, performer of many kinds of acts or possessor of many kinds of wisdom, Indra, these praises of ours go forth to you, again and again; the root nu has here the sense of motion. The illustration: as mothers, cows, go quickly to a calf that is in the house, so do they. Or else: these words of ours sound toward him, they praise him, as cows low in the direction of the calf.
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O performer of acts of many kinds
- वत्सं न (*vatsaṃ na*)—as they run affectionately to their calves and join them
- इमा गिरः (*imā giraḥ*)—these praises recited by us
- प्र णोनुवुः (*pra ṇonuvuḥ*)—come and join, at every step
O Indra, performer of acts of many kinds, as mother cows run affectionately to their calves and join them, so these praises recited by us come and join you, at every step, turned toward you.
Indra, performer of many exploits, these our praises repeatedly recur to you as parent (cows) to their young.

O Indra, your friendship is दूणाशं (*dūṇāśaṃ*), hard to destroy, that is, it cannot be destroyed; the meaning is that it is exceedingly firm. Therefore, O hero, you are a गौः (*gauḥ*) for him who desires cattle for himself: you are the giver of cattle; the word for the effect is used for the cause by figurative usage. Likewise for him who desires horses for himself, you are a horse: you are the giver of horses.
- दूणाशं (*dūṇāśaṃ*)—is not to be destroyed easily
- गौः असि (*gauḥ asi*)—you are the giver of cattle
- अश्वः भव (*aśvaḥ bhava*)—you are the giver of horses
O Indra, your friendship is not to be destroyed easily. O valiant Indra, you bestow cattle on those who desire cattle, and horses on those who desire horses.
Your friendship, Indra, is not easily lost : you, hero, are (the giver of) cattle to him who desires cattle, (of) horses to him who desires horses.

O Indra, you who are so renowned, rejoice (मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*)) with your own body, gladdened by drinking the Soma (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)); rejoice for great wealth, that is, for the sake of riches; the word हि (*hi*) is a filler. And do not hand over your worshipper to the power of the reviler.
- सः (*saḥ*)—(O Indra) you who are renowned
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—satisfied by the drinking of Soma
- न करः (*na karaḥ*)—do not give up
O Indra, you who are renowned, attain contentment with a body satisfied by the drinking of Soma, for the gain of great wealth. Do not give up him who praises you to the reviler, the enemy.
Delight your person with the (beverage of the) libation (offered) for the sake of great treasure : subject not your worshipper to his reviler.

O Girvaṇas, Indra, who are to be adored with songs: at every pressing of the Soma, these praises of ours reach you (नक्षंते (*nakṣaṃte*) means they pervade). As milch cows (धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*), those that give milk) reach their calf, quickly pervading it, so do our praises reach you.
- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—O Indra, who are honoured with praises
- वत्सं न (*vatsaṃ na*)—as they come and join their calves
- सुते सुते (*sute sute*)—whenever the Soma juice is pressed
- इमा गिरः (*imā giraḥ*)—these praise-words of ours
O Indra, who are honoured with praises, as milch cows come and join their calves, so, whenever the Soma juice is pressed, these praise-words of ours come and pervade you.
These our praises tend, as the libations are repeatedly poured out, eagerly to you who are gratified by praise, as the milch cows (hasten) to their calves.

O Indra, you who wear out and exhaust many enemies: may the praise of us, the many worshippers, reach you; this is the word to be supplied. Of what kind are we? We are those who, in the sacrifice (विवाचि (*vivāci*)) in which there are various kinds of speech, consisting of stotras and śastras, make you vigorous (वाजयतां (*vājayatāṃ*)), that is, strong or possessed of strength, with food (वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)), meaning with the foods that are the oblations.
- विवाचि (*vivāci*)—(O Indra) in the sacrifice accompanied by many kinds of praises
- वाजेभिः (*vājebhiḥ*)—with the foods that take the form of oblations
- वाजयतां (*vājayatāṃ*)—of those who make you powerful
- पुराणां (*purāṇāṃ*)—of those who are many in number
- स्तोतृणां (*stotṛṇāṃ*)—of us, the praisers, (may the praises)
- पुरुतमः (*purutamaḥ*)—come and reach you, who kill many enemies

O Indra, may the praises of us, the praisers, who are many in number and who make you powerful with the foods that take the form of oblations in the sacrifice accompanied by many kinds of praises, come and reach you, who kill many enemies.
May the praises of many worshippers offered at the sacrifice, (accompanied) by (sacrificial) viands. invigorate you, destroyer of multitudes.

O Indra, may our praise (स्तोमः (*stomaḥ*)), which is the best bearer (वोढृतमो (*voḍhṛtamo*)), be nearest to you. And you urge us on (हिनु (*hinu*) means impel) to great (महे (*mahe*)) wealth. ⟨NOTE:55⟩
notes: ವಾಹಿಷ್ಠಃ glossed in the Kannada as ಅತಿಶಯವಾಗಿ ಔನ್ನತ್ಯವನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುವ "having exaltedness in the highest degree"; Sāyaṇa has ವೋಢೃತಮಃ "best bearer"

en: - वाहिष्ठः (*vāhiṣṭhaḥ*)—possessing exaltedness in the highest degree
O Indra, may our praise, which has exaltedness in the highest degree, have come very near to you. Impel us towards great wealth.
May our most elevating praise be near, Indra, to you, and urge us to (the acquirement of) great riches.

Bṛbu is the name of the carpenter of the Paṇis. Bharadvāja, having obtained wealth from him, extolled his gift with this triplet. This is also recalled by Manu: भरद्वाजः क्षुधार्तस्तु सपुत्रो विजने वने । बर्हीर्गाः प्रतिजग्राह बृबोस्तक्ष्णो महायशाः ॥ (*bharadvājaḥ kṣudhārtastu saputro vijane vane | barhīrgāḥ pratijagrāha bṛbostakṣṇo mahāyaśāḥ ‖*) (Ma 10-107) **GLOSS** ⟨NOTE:56⟩ The Paṇis are so called from trading (पणनात् (*paṇanāt*)): they are merchants, or else asuras of this name. Of them Bṛbu the carpenter has taken his stand (स्थलेऽध्यस्थात् (*sthale 'dhyasthāt*)) on the loftiest (वर्षिष्टे (*varṣiṣṭe*)) place, one raised up like a head (मूर्धन् (*mūrdhan*)). He is गांग्यः (*gāṃgyaḥ*), born on the high bank of the Gaṅgā, and, like a कक्षॆ (*kakṣè*), he is broad (उरुः (*uruḥ*)), spread wide. The meaning is: though low by birth, by being a giver he becomes the best everywhere.
notes: abbreviation ಮ printed before ೧೦-೧೦೭

en: - कक्षो न (*kakṣo na*)—like the exceedingly high bank
- अधि अस्थात् (*adhi asthāt*)—has obtained a position; (the position)
- उरुः (*uruḥ*)—he has also obtained wide fame

Like the exceedingly high bank of the river Gaṅgā, the carpenter named Bṛbu, among all the Paṇis, has obtained the most excellent and exceedingly lofty position, and has attained exceedingly wide fame.
Bribu presided over the high places of the Panis, like the elevated bank of the Ganges.

The gift (रातिः (*rātiḥ*)) of Bṛbu, who goes swiftly like the wind, is auspicious (भद्रा (*bhadrā*), that is, benevolent) and consists of a thousand; at once, at the very time of the praise, it gives the wealth I desired to me (मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)), who am asking for a gift (दानाय (*dānāya*)) and desire it (मंहते (*maṃhate*)). The connection is with that Bṛbu in the following Ṛk.
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at the very time of praise
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—to me, who desire a gift
- मंहते (*maṃhate*)—and who seek wealth, was given (such a Bṛbu is renowned)
Such a Bṛbu is renowned, whose auspicious gift, numbering a thousand, swift like the wind, was given at the very time of the praise to me, who desired a gift and sought wealth.
Of whom, prompt as the wind, the liberal donation of thousands (of cattle) has been quickly given to (me) soliciting a gift.

That Bṛbu is always well (सु (*su*), meaning excellently) praised (गृणंति (*gṛṇaṃti*), that is, they extol, they laud) by all those who are ours (नः (*naḥ*)), the अर्यः (*aryaḥ*) who stir up praises, the praisers. Of what kind is he? He is the greatest giver of a thousandfold wealth (सहस्रदातमं (*sahasradātamaṃ*)); wise (सूरिं (*sūriṃ*)), or else an impeller; and the greatest sharer (सहस्रसातमं (*sahasrasātamaṃ*)) of a thousandfold praise or wealth. ⟨NOTE:57⟩
notes: ಅರ್ಯಃ glossed in the Kannada as ಆರ್ಯಃ ಪೂಜ್ಯರು "venerable"; Sāyaṇa has ಸ್ತುತೀನಾಮಿರಯಿತಾರಃ "those who stir up praises"

en: - सहस्रदातमं (*sahasradātamaṃ*)—the giver of wealth numbering a thousand
- सहस्रसातमं (*sahasrasātamaṃ*)—and the sharer in wealth numbering a thousand

That same Bṛbu, the giver of wealth numbering a thousand, the wise one, the lord of wealth numbering a thousand, is praised always, exceedingly and in the highest degree, by the praisers, who belong to us, all of them venerable.
Whom, therefore, we all, who are the profferers and bestowers of praise ever commend, as the pious Bribu, the donor of thousands (of cattle) the recciver of thousands (of laudations).

We singers (कारवः (*kāravaḥ*)), for the sake of the sharing of food (साता (*sātā*), that is, when there is a cause for sharing), call on you alone, O Indra, with praises. O Indra, protector of the good and the best, other men too call on you in the encounters with enemies (वृत्रेषु (*vṛtreṣu*), the obstructing foes) for the conquest of them. And in the battles (काष्ठासु (*kāṣṭhāsu*)) connected with the horse, where the horse stands having advanced, those who desire to fight call on you alone. Therefore we too call on you alone: this is the meaning.
- सत्पतिं (*satpatiṃ*)—the protector of good men and the best
- वृत्रेषु (*vṛtreṣu*)—at the time of fighting with enemies (they call you for help)
